feed.title: ICF Completes Acquisition of Creative Systems and Consulting
feed.summary: ICF (NASDAQ: ICFI) has announced the completion of its acquisition of Creative Systems and Consulting, a leading provider of IT modernization and digital transformation solutions for U.S. federal agencies. Creative, founded in 2010, brings expertise in Salesforce, Microsoft, and ServiceNow platforms, which complements ICF's existing capabilities. This acquisition aims to enhance ICF's digital transformation services for its federal government clients.

feed.title: Apple becomes first company to hit $3 trillion market value, then slips
feed.summary: Apple Inc. briefly touched a $3 trillion stock market valuation on January 3, 2022, becoming the first company to reach this milestone, fueled by investor confidence in its product pipeline and expansion into new markets like automated cars and virtual reality. Although its market capitalization slipped just below $3 trillion by day's end, the achievement highlights the company's strong fundamentals and consumer loyalty for its iPhones, MacBooks, and services. The stock has seen significant growth since the first iPhone launch in 2007, and under CEO Tim Cook, Apple has successfully diversified its revenue streams beyond the iPhone.

feed.title: AMD Unveils New Ryzen Mobile Processors Uniting “Zen 3+” core with AMD RDNA 2 Graphics in Powerhouse Design
feed.summary: AMD has announced its new Ryzen 6000 Series processors for laptops, combining the "Zen 3+" core architecture with RDNA 2 graphics for enhanced performance and battery life. Additionally, AMD introduced the Ryzen 7 5800X3D desktop processor with 3D V-Cache technology for superior gaming and preview previewed the upcoming Ryzen 7000 Series with "Zen 4" architecture. These announcements highlight AMD's focus on innovation across mobile and desktop computing, emphasizing efficiency, graphics capabilities, and security features.

feed.title: An Under the Radar High Quality ETF
feed.summary: The Fidelity Quality Factor ETF (FQAL) received a five-star rating from CFRA, outperforming its peers and the S&P 500 in 2021 despite its smaller asset size. The fund focuses on free cash flow and return on invested capital with a sector-neutral approach, and CFRA expects it to continue outperforming. Eight of its top-10 holdings are considered undervalued by CFRA analysts.

feed.title: Fully Automated AI Collision Repair Estimating ‘Not There Yet’
feed.summary: Representatives from Mitchell International, CCC Intelligent Solutions, and Tractable discussed the current state and limitations of AI in collision repair estimating at a Collision Industry Conference (CIC) event. While AI can improve consistency and efficiency for low-severity claims and total loss triage, full automation is still "not there yet" for complex repairs. Experts emphasized the need for human interaction and the integration of OEM data to achieve accurate estimates.

feed.title: 3 BYOD security risks and how to prevent them
feed.summary: The increasing adoption of Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) policies introduces significant security challenges for organizations, despite offering cost savings and flexibility. Key risks include data theft stemming from personal logins and cloud synchronization, unclear security protocols leading to shadow IT and employee-driven breaches, and the prevalence of mobile malware. Effective prevention requires robust mobile device management policies, including encryption, application blacklisting, regular data backups, and thorough employee security training.

feed.title: Hasbro Promotes Chris Cocks to CEO
feed.summary: Hasbro has named Chris Cocks as its new CEO, succeeding the late Brian Goldner and interim CEO Rich Stoddart. Cocks, previously president and COO of Wizards of the Coast and digital gaming, will focus on evolving Hasbro’s brand blueprint strategy and generating growth. Eric Nyman has been appointed president and COO of Hasbro, while Stoddart will become chair of the board.

feed.title: Stellantis taps Amazon to bolster software plans, will sell it EV vans
feed.summary: Stellantis announced a multi-year partnership with Amazon to enhance its software-driven vehicle offerings and services. The collaboration includes deploying Amazon software in Stellantis vehicles, training engineers, and making Amazon the first commercial customer for the battery-electric Ram ProMaster van. This move aims to significantly increase Stellantis's annual revenue from software-enabled products and subscriptions by 2030, transforming the automaker into a technologically savvy mobility company.

feed.title: $20 Billion In 2022: Google Pays Apple For Not Launching Its Own Search Engine?
feed.summary: A class action lawsuit has been filed against Apple and Google, alleging an illegal agreement where Google pays Apple billions annually to remain the default search engine on Apple devices and prevents Apple from developing its own search engine. The lawsuit claims this arrangement violates US antitrust law, stifles competition, and inflates advertising rates. While both companies have been discreet about the exact figures, estimates suggest Google could pay Apple around $20 billion in 2022, accounting for a significant portion of Apple's annual earnings.

feed.title: Iberdrola optimizes working capital with SAP® Real-Time Treasury
feed.summary: Iberdrola, a global leader in renewable energy, has partnered with J.P. Morgan to implement the SAP® Real-Time Treasury app. This integration provides Iberdrola with real-time visibility into their global cash positions, streamlines treasury operations, and enhances their ability to respond to market changes. The solution, powered by J.P. Morgan's Treasury Services APIs, has migrated Iberdrola from daily reporting to instant access to financial data, optimizing their working capital management.

feed.title: Octo Acquires Digital Transformation Leader B3 Group
feed.summary: Octo, a federal IT modernization provider, has acquired B3 Group, Inc., a digital transformation company specializing in low-code/no-code platforms and cloud engineering. This acquisition expands Octo's reach into the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), bolstering its position in the federal health market and enhancing its ability to provide advanced IT modernization services across various federal agencies. The integration of B3's expertise and programs, including the Digital Transformation Center (DTC) contract, will strengthen Octo's oLabs environment and offer improved digital solutions to federal customers.

feed.title: Qualcomm, Microsoft partner on metaverse chip for AR glasses
feed.summary: Qualcomm and Microsoft are collaborating on custom chips for lightweight augmented reality (AR) glasses, targeting both consumers and businesses for metaverse applications. The partnership aims to integrate these chips with Microsoft's Mesh software for virtual presence and Qualcomm's Snapdragon Spaces for AR functions like spatial mapping and hand-tracking. Though no release date was provided, the initiative seeks to advance wearable AR devices for broader adoption.

feed.title: Western Union looks to improve data quality with Talend
feed.summary: Western Union's chief data officer, Thomas Mazzaferro, details the company's cloud data migration strategy and its reliance on Talend for data quality. The financial services vendor has consolidated over 20 petabytes of data into an AWS-based single data lake with Snowflake, leveraging Talend for ingestion, ETL, and data quality monitoring. Mazzaferro emphasizes the importance of data measurement, accountability, and a collaborative approach between business and technology teams to address data quality issues in near real-time.

feed.title: XPENG Integrates Text-to-Speech Service From Microsoft in P7 Smart Sedan
feed.summary: XPENG has upgraded its P7 smart sedan's auto-grade voice assistant by integrating Microsoft's custom neural voice capability, based on Neural Text-to-Speech (TTS) from Azure AI. This over-the-air update for P7 customers in China addresses challenges like network jitter and data consumption using caching while enhancing speech quality and naturalness. The collaboration allows for more lifelike voice fidelity and scenario-specific applicability, with future plans to roll out this technology to other XPENG models.

feed.title: Zoom as a video production platform shows it knows that online events aren't going away
feed.summary: Zoom's recent acquisition of Liminal, a small software company specializing in video production solutions for virtual events, signals a strategic shift towards becoming a robust platform for highly produced online events. This move, following a failed acquisition attempt and the recognized permanence of hybrid work, positions Zoom to expand its role beyond basic video conferencing. Liminal's technology, including ZoomOSC and ZoomISO, enhances Zoom's offerings for professional event production, allowing for greater control and customization of virtual gatherings.

feed.title: What Crypto-related ETFs Could Hit the US Market in 2022?
feed.summary: The article discusses the potential for various crypto-related ETFs, particularly metaverse products, to launch in the US market in 2022, while the approval of spot bitcoin and ether futures products remains uncertain. Industry experts express apprehension about the immediate investability of metaverse ETFs due to potential crossover in holdings and a lack of pure-play names. There's also skepticism regarding the SEC's approval of a spot bitcoin ETF in 2022, with some analysts expecting an ether futures-based ETF to gain approval sooner.

feed.title: Hasbro Names Former Dungeons & Dragons Exec Chris Cocks As New CEO
feed.summary: Hasbro has appointed Chris Cocks, formerly the president and chief operating officer of Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming division, as its new CEO, effective February 25. Cocks succeeds the late Brian Goldner and interim CEO Rich Stoddart. Under Cocks' previous leadership, Hasbro's Dungeons & Dragons and Magic: The Gathering franchises generated substantial revenue, showcasing his ability to drive growth in the gaming sector.

feed.title: What Is Antivirus Company Norton Even Doing Mining Crypto on Your Computer?
feed.summary: Norton, an antivirus company, has introduced a new feature called "Norton Crypto" that allows users to mine cryptocurrencies. This move is interpreted as a shift from its traditional antivirus business, which many now consider less essential due to built-in operating system security features and the perceived bloat of security software. The article questions the efficacy and relevance of traditional antivirus programs in the current cybersecurity landscape, suggesting that Norton's pivot into crypto mining might reflect a struggle to stay relevant, similar to Kodak's past foray into cryptocurrency.

feed.title: 'Creating a loose federation': Stagwell's Jason Reid is buying pieces of the next agency holding company
feed.summary: Jason Reid, Stagwell's chief investment officer, is actively acquiring digital-first assets, planning to invest $50-100 million annually to expand the holding company's offerings geographically and across disciplines. Stagwell aims to differentiate itself from competitors by creating a "loose federation" of agencies to win local businesses and offer comprehensive marketing services. Penn and Reid believe their strategic approach to acquisitions and focus on growth for acquired businesses gives them an edge over private equity firms and rival holding companies.

feed.title: FOS PM: NYT Buys The Athletic
feed.summary: The New York Times has acquired the sports subscription site The Athletic for $550 million in an all-cash deal, aiming to boost its digital subscriber count to 10 million by 2025. This acquisition comes as The Athletic, despite having 1.2 million subscribers, has yet to turn a profit. Separately, online sports betting is set to launch in New York with four major sportsbooks, and Authentic Brands Group, owner of Reebok, has canceled its IPO plans, opting for private funding rounds.

feed.title: Machine Customers Will Decide Who Gets Their Trillion-Dollar Business. Is It You?
feed.summary: The article explores the rise of "machine customers" and their potential to drive a trillion-dollar business opportunity. It outlines how these nonhuman entities, ranging from bound to autonomous customers, make purchasing decisions differently from humans by being transparent, processing vast amounts of data, and prioritizing efficiency over emotional loyalty. Businesses must adapt their corporate strategy, sales, marketing, and data analytics to cater to this evolving market.

feed.title: JVAL Stock Price | JPMorgan U.S. Value Factor ETF
feed.summary: This article provides detailed information about the JPMorgan U.S. Value Factor ETF (JVAL), including its current stock price, trading exchange (NYSE), and comprehensive financial metrics such as dividend yield, expense ratio, and market capitalization. It also offers technical analysis insights and lists the ETF's top holdings, outlining its investment strategy as a value-focused equity fund targeting the U.S. market.

feed.title: Updating My Favorite Performance Chart For 2021
feed.summary: Ben Carlson updates his asset allocation quilt for 2021, analyzing the performance of various asset classes over the last decade. He highlights REITs' surprising strong performance, the ongoing struggles of commodities despite recent gains, and the consistent outperformance of the S&P 500. The article also discusses the impact of diversification and the impressive long-term returns of U.S. stocks even when including the 2008 financial crisis.

feed.title: Payments firms see slam dunk opportunity with sports venues
feed.summary: The sports and events industry is becoming a major focus for digital payments companies, which are introducing new technologies to enhance the fan experience and gather valuable data. The push for cashless and contactless transactions was accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic, leading to the adoption of mobile ordering, self-service kiosks, and checkout-free options in stadiums and arenas. These advancements not only speed up transactions but also provide venues with crucial insights into fan behavior and purchasing habits.

feed.title: JPM 2022: Johnson & Johnson links up with Microsoft to cloud-connect its digital surgery programs
feed.summary: Johnson & Johnson has partnered with Microsoft to build a cloud-connected software ecosystem for its digital surgery initiatives. Microsoft will serve as J&J's preferred cloud provider, integrating various medical devices and services, including surgical planning, robotic procedures, and rehabilitation programs. This collaboration will leverage Microsoft's Azure services, artificial intelligence, and machine learning, impacting J&J's Velys joint reconstruction system and Auris Health's Monarch endoscopy robots, and setting the stage for the delayed Ottava general surgery robot.

feed.title: Nvidia buys high-performance computing cluster management software provider Bright Computing
feed.summary: Nvidia has acquired Bright Computing Inc., a company specializing in software for managing high-performance computing (HPC) systems. This acquisition aims to enhance Nvidia's offerings in the HPC market, integrating Bright's Cluster Manager into Nvidia's software stack to provide more complete infrastructure platforms for accelerated computing. The move is seen as another step in Nvidia's evolution from a chip company to a comprehensive solution provider for data centers, particularly as HPC and AI workloads converge.

feed.title: Oracle Corp. stock rises Monday, outperforms market
feed.summary: Oracle Corp. (ORCL) stock increased by 2.02% to $89.28 on Monday, outperforming the broader market downturn where the S&P 500 Index and Dow Jones Industrial Average fell. This marks the stock's second consecutive day of gains, although it remains $17.06 short of its 52-week high. Oracle's performance was mixed compared to competitors like Microsoft, Adobe, and Salesforce.com, and trading volume exceeded its 50-day average.

feed.title: Johnson & Johnson Medical Devices Companies: Reimagining the patient journey in a digital era - Source
feed.summary: Johnson & Johnson Medical Devices Companies (JJMDC) and Microsoft have entered a multiyear collaboration to reimagine the patient journey in a digital era. Microsoft will become JJMDC’s preferred cloud provider for its digital surgery solutions, with the goal of using AI, machine learning, and data insights to improve patient outcomes, increase consistency in care, and enhance surgical performance. The partnership aims to connect medical devices, patient records, and hospital information systems through Azure to provide comprehensive patient views and predictive maintenance capabilities.

feed.title: Palo Alto Networks Joins Microsoft 365 Networking Partner Program
feed.summary: Palo Alto Networks announced its integration into the Microsoft 365 Networking Partner Program, aiming to provide secure and efficient connectivity for Microsoft 365 users through its Prisma Access service. This collaboration ensures an optimal user experience aligned with Microsoft's connectivity principles, particularly for hybrid workforces. Prisma Access offers a cloud-delivered security platform that meets Microsoft 365 requirements, enabling Zero Trust access and robust threat protection for enterprise customers.

feed.title: Datto Hires Splunk, Qlik Veteran Brooke Cunningham as CMO -
feed.summary: Datto has appointed Brooke Cunningham, a veteran from Splunk and Qlik, as its new Chief Marketing Officer. This strategic hire aligns with Datto's ongoing expansion beyond its traditional storage offerings into cloud-based software and security solutions for Managed Service Providers (MSPs). Cunningham's experience in scaling businesses and nurturing partner ecosystems, particularly in the security technology sector, is expected to support Datto's accelerated growth and its commitment to the MSP community.

feed.title: Former Cerence CEO headed to California with new top role
feed.summary: Sanjay Dhawan, the former CEO of Burlington-based Cerence Inc., who abruptly resigned last year, has been appointed to a new top role in California, leading SymphonyAI. Dhawan previously led Cerence's spin-out from Nuance Communications Inc. in 2019. His new position reveals the reason behind his sudden departure from Cerence.

feed.title: Microsoft, Johnson & Johnson Medical Device Companies team up on digital surgery ecosystem
feed.summary: Johnson & Johnson Medical Device Companies (JJMDC) and Microsoft have announced a collaboration to expand JJMDC's digital surgery ecosystem. Utilizing Microsoft's Azure cloud platform, the partnership aims to develop a surgical-monitoring dashboard, enhance connectivity, and accelerate the development of digital tools through AI, machine learning, and data insights. This initiative is expected to personalize surgical care and improve workflows across the entire patient journey.

feed.title: Take-Two Interactive CEO makes the case for his $12.7 billion takeover of Zynga
feed.summary: Take-Two Interactive's CEO, Strauss Zelnick, defended the company's $12.7 billion acquisition of Zynga, refuting investor concerns over the high premium paid. The merger, the most expensive in video game history, is expected to shift Take-Two's business significantly towards mobile gaming, with 50% of combined fiscal 2023 net bookings anticipated from mobile titles. Zelnick sees this as an opportunity to bring Take-Two's popular intellectual properties like Grand Theft Auto to mobile platforms, though not necessarily as direct ports of full console games.

feed.title: Welcoming the Post-Zoom Era
feed.summary: The article discusses the impending end of the "Zoom era," noting a waning enthusiasm for constant video conferencing, even among those previously reliant on it. Author Jonathan Bartlett observes that people are increasingly opting out of Zoom meetings and classes, highlighting the draining nature of online interaction compared to in-person engagement. He suggests that organizations must soon decide whether to be primarily remote or in-person, and for remote setups, managers will need to minimize Zoom time and find alternative ways to foster team cohesion to prevent a decline in loyalty.

feed.title: Microsoft announces new research and technology to empower millions of frontline workers
feed.summary: Microsoft has released new research and technology, including updates to Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Viva, aimed at empowering millions of frontline workers globally. The company saw 400% growth in monthly active Teams usage by frontline workers since March 2020, and the new features address challenges identified in a Work Trend Index report, such as communication gaps and the need for better training and technology integration. These developments aim to modernize workflows, enhance job performance, and improve workplace culture for the 2 billion frontline workers worldwide.

feed.title: Lloyds aims to save £800m with shift to cloud, DXC to lead modernisation
feed.summary: Lloyd's, a major insurance marketplace, has launched an ambitious digital transformation program called "Future at Lloyd's" to move core applications to the cloud and digitize paper-based processes. DXC Technology has been selected as the lead IT provider, with AWS as the primary cloud provider. This initiative is expected to save £800 million in operating costs for brokers, underwriters, and partners.

feed.title: What’s Changed: 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems
feed.summary: This article analyzes the 2021 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Cloud Database Management Systems, highlighting key market trends and changes from the previous report. It details Gartner's definition of the market, significant additions and removals of vendors, and the evolving positions of major players like Amazon, Microsoft, Oracle, Google, Snowflake, and Databricks within the Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players quadrants. The report emphasizes the increasing shift to cloud platforms, the impact of multicloud strategies, and the growing importance of various data models and use cases in the CDBMS market.

feed.title: TransUnion Africa appoints Morris Maina as CEO for Kenya
feed.summary: TransUnion Africa has appointed Morris Maina, a former Safaricom and Microsoft executive, as its new CEO for Kenya. Maina, who started his tenure on January 10, 2022, will focus on growing the company's fraud and risk solutions in the Kenyan market. TransUnion Africa operates in eight countries and provides commercial, consumer, insurance, and auto risk information solutions, aiming to help businesses make informed decisions and consumers manage their credit.

feed.title: DevOps Tool Market 2022 Outstanding Growth Scope Witnessed
feed.summary: The global DevOps Tool market is projected to reach USD 6881.6 million by 2026, growing from USD 4092.1 million in 2020 at a CAGR of 13.9% over five years. This report by Infinity Business Insights analyzes key players, market trends, and the impact of COVID-19, providing insights for investors and businesses to achieve market growth. The study covers product types like DevOps Ready, Enabled, and Capable, and applications across various sectors including IT, Telecom, BFSI, and Government.

feed.title: T-Mobile uses RPA in Power Automate to integrate systems during Sprint merger
feed.summary: T-Mobile leveraged Robotic Process Automation (RPA) capabilities in Microsoft Power Automate to integrate its Orbit app with Sprint's legacy Quickbase system following their merger. This approach addressed challenges like data latency, manual processes, and data entry errors that could not be solved with traditional APIs. By using RPA, T-Mobile significantly improved efficiency, reduced processing time by 12x, and eliminated human data entry errors, thereby allowing analysts to focus on more strategic tasks.

feed.title: BlackRock CEO Larry Fink says stakeholder capitalism is not 'woke'
feed.summary: Larry Fink, CEO of BlackRock, defended stakeholder capitalism against criticism, asserting it is not "woke" but rather a strategy for generating profit. In his annual letter to CEOs, Fink emphasized that focusing on sustainability is a capitalist and fiduciary responsibility, not a political or ideological agenda. He also clarified that BlackRock's approach doesn't involve divestment from fossil fuels, despite pressure from environmental groups, and noted the firm's engagement in China as a significant opportunity.

feed.title: Child Labor and the Human Rights Violations Embedded in Producing Technology
feed.summary: This article examines the pervasive issue of child labor in the technology sector's supply chain, particularly concerning cobalt mining for batteries, and the broader human rights violations involved. It critiques the current international legal framework for corporate accountability, highlighting its inadequacies in prosecuting multinational corporations. The author advocates for new international forums and expanded definitions of corporate responsibility to hold both direct violators and corporate benefactors accountable for human rights abuses.

feed.title: NPD: The top 20 best-selling games of 2021 in the U.S.
feed.summary: The NPD Group has released its list of the top 20 best-selling games in the U.S. for 2021, revealing Call of Duty: Vanguard as the top seller. The report highlights the continued dominance of established franchises like Call of Duty and Pokémon, with several games from previous years remaining strong sellers. Analyst Mat Piscatella noted record-breaking sales for the Pokémon franchise and Resident Evil series, alongside the successful Xbox debut of MLB The Show 21.

feed.title: What Microsoft’s US$68b acquisition of Activision Blizzard means for Vancouver
feed.summary: Microsoft's US$68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard will bring Vancouver's Activision subsidiaries, such as Demonware Canada Ltd. and a Treyarch Corp. office, under the same corporate umbrella as Microsoft's Vancouver-based studio, The Coalition. This deal highlights the ongoing growth in B.C.'s gaming sector, which saw a 19% increase in jobs and a 39% rise in companies between 2019 and 2021, generating $4.3 billion in revenue for Canada in 2021. The acquisition will impact Vancouver's gaming landscape by consolidating several studios under one major tech giant.

feed.title: Microsoft to acquire Activision Blizzard to bring the joy and community of gaming to everyone, across every device
feed.summary: Microsoft announced its plans to acquire Activision Blizzard, a major player in game development, to expand its gaming business across mobile, PC, console, and cloud platforms. This acquisition will make Microsoft the world's third-largest gaming company by revenue and include iconic franchises like “Warcraft,” “Diablo,” “Call of Duty,” and “Candy Crush,” aiming to accelerate the development of metaverse platforms. Satya Nadella emphasized the investment in world-class content, community, and cloud to create a safe, inclusive, and accessible gaming experience for all.

feed.title: Microsoft Buys Activision: 3 Reasons Why The Deal Makes Sense (NASDAQ:MSFT)
feed.summary: Microsoft's planned acquisition of Activision Blizzard for $69 billion is analyzed, with the author presenting three key reasons why the deal is strategically beneficial for Microsoft shareholders. These reasons include the potential for increased recurring revenues, opportunities in the burgeoning metaverse, and a value-creating use of Microsoft's substantial cash reserves. The article suggests that despite skepticism often surrounding M&A, this particular acquisition makes sound business sense.

feed.title: Rackspace Technology All Set to Acquire Just Analytics
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology announced its agreement to acquire Just Analytics, a leading provider of cloud-based data, analytics, and AI services from the Asia Pacific and Japan region. This acquisition enhances Rackspace's professional services, adding in-demand cloud-based data, analytics, and AI capabilities while strengthening ties within the Microsoft Azure ecosystem. Just Analytics, known for its proprietary data platform Guzzle and strong customer service, will retain its brand for the foreseeable future.

feed.title: Oracle opens data centre to provide cloud services across Africa
feed.summary: Oracle has launched its first data center in South Africa, providing local cloud services across the African continent to better compete with rivals like Microsoft and Amazon. The new data center in Johannesburg is Oracle's 37th "cloud region" globally, with plans to reach 44 this year. This move caters to the increasing demand for faster computing from African banks and telecom firms, despite challenges such as high power prices and frequent outages in South Africa.

feed.title: The Threat Landscape in 2021
feed.summary: Symantec, a division of Broadcom Software, reviewed the major cyber threats of 2021, highlighting ransomware, supply chain attacks, exploitation of public-facing application vulnerabilities, and attacks on critical infrastructure. While ransomware attack numbers decreased, targeted ransomware incidents increased significantly, fueled by initial access brokers and ransomware-as-a-service models. The report details prominent attacks like SolarWinds, Kaseya, and Colonial Pipeline, emphasizing the evolving tactics of threat actors and the rising impact on organizations and society.

feed.title: Employee surveillance is exploding with remote work—and could be the new norm
feed.summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the adoption of employee surveillance software, with 60% of large companies using these technologies by the end of 2021, compared to 30% pre-pandemic. This expansion of monitoring into employees' homes raises significant concerns about privacy, trust, and the blurring of work-life boundaries. Experts warn of "function creep," where temporary surveillance measures become permanent, and highlight the urgent need for new legal protections for workers' privacy, as existing laws are largely weak and inadequate for the evolving landscape of remote work.

feed.title: Smithsonian Latino Center Receives $1 Million Gift From Microsoft Corp.
feed.summary: The Smithsonian Latino Center has received a $1 million gift from Microsoft Corp. to support the Molina Family Latino Gallery, which is the first Smithsonian gallery dedicated to exploring Latino history, culture, and identity in the U.S. This donation will also aid in the development of the future National Museum of the American Latino. The gallery's first exhibition, "!Presente! A Latino History of the United States," will feature bilingual exhibitions, public and educational programs, and online resources made possible by Microsoft's contribution.

feed.title: Tomonari Sato: Why I joined Cloudflare and why I’m helping Cloudflare grow in Japan
feed.summary: Tomonari Sato, with 35 years of experience in the IT industry, has joined Cloudflare as Vice-President and Managing Director in Japan to expand its presence and customer base. He believes Cloudflare's solutions are crucial for Japan's digital transformation, aligning with the government's "Cloud By Default" policy. Sato is enthusiastic about contributing to Cloudflare's mission and helping Japanese organizations leverage its global network for security, performance, and cost efficiency.

feed.title: Oracle opens South African cloud region in Johannesburg
feed.summary: Oracle has launched its first cloud region in Africa, located in Johannesburg, South Africa, making it the company's 37th global cloud region. The company aims to expand to 44 cloud regions by the end of 2022, with plans for further expansion in Africa potentially starting next year, focusing on areas like West Africa. This move places Oracle alongside other major cloud providers like Microsoft and AWS, which already have a presence on the continent, as the demand for data center infrastructure in Africa continues to grow significantly.

feed.title: Rackspace to acquire Singapore-based Just Analytics
feed.summary: Rackspace Technology announced its acquisition of Just Analytics, a Singapore-based provider of cloud-based data, analytics, and AI services. While the acquisition amount was not disclosed, Rackspace plans to retain the "Just Analytics" name due to its recognition in the Microsoft Azure Data Analytics market. This move aims to enhance Rackspace's professional services and expand its data, analytics, and AI capabilities.

feed.title: How to Invest in the Top 100 U.S. ESG Companies
feed.summary: The article discusses the 2022 list of top 100 U.S. ESG companies compiled by Just Capital, highlighting major movements like Alphabet's rise and Meta's fall. It explains the methodology behind the rankings, which prioritize issues important to Americans, and introduces the Goldman Sachs JUST U.S. Large Cap Equity ETF (JUST) as a way to invest in companies demonstrating "just business behavior."

feed.title: What is HPC-as-a-service and why does it matter?
feed.summary: High Performance Compute-as-a-service (HPCaaS) is emerging as a critical cloud service, offering hardware, software, and expertise to process demanding workloads like big data analytics. This service addresses the challenges companies face with in-house HPC, such as high costs and specialized staffing, by leveraging cloud infrastructure from providers like IBM and Microsoft Azure. While offering benefits like faster technology integration and dynamic management, HPCaaS also presents challenges related to security, licensing costs, and data transfer, though experts believe these will be overcome by continued innovation, with the market projected to reach $17 billion by 2026.

feed.title: Rate Hikes Might Bring Quality ETFs Into Focus
feed.summary: As interest rate hike jitters grip markets and previously high-flying growth stocks falter, quality-focused investments like the Invesco S&P 500 Quality ETF (SPHQ) are gaining attention. SPHQ, which holds profitable, cash-rich companies like Apple and Microsoft, is outperforming broader benchmarks. This trend suggests a market shift towards financially sound companies as the Federal Reserve prepares for a rate tightening cycle.

feed.title: The untold story of zero trust and data privacy
feed.summary: This article discusses the critical intersection of zero trust architectures and data privacy, highlighting how engineering data protection into enterprise systems can significantly reduce attack surfaces and improve compliance. It emphasizes the growing consumer concern about data privacy, evidenced by surveys and increasing legislative action, and advocates for Zero Trust Network Architecture (ZTNA) as a robust solution to protect sensitive data from both internal and external threats, ultimately benefiting business agility and reputation.

feed.title: Check Point Software’s 2022 Security Report: Global Cyber Pandemic’s Magnitude Revealed
feed.summary: Check Point Research's 2022 Security Report reveals a 50% increase in cyber-attacks worldwide in 2021, with the Education and Research sector being the most targeted. The report highlights a "supply chain attack frenzy," disruptions to everyday life, and evolving threats against cloud services and mobile devices. Despite the surge in attacks, the report also notes increasing efforts by governments and law enforcement to combat ransomware groups.

feed.title: Microsoft secures IPs like Call of Duty and Candy Crash to boost its metaverse ambitions, analyst says
feed.summary: Microsoft's $68.7 billion acquisition of Activision Blizzard is seen as a strategic move to bolster its metaverse ambitions, according to analyst Joost Rietveld. The deal secures popular gaming franchises like Call of Duty and Candy Crush, potentially differentiating Microsoft's Game Pass service and influencing cross-platform availability. While Microsoft has committed to honoring existing agreements, allowing Call of Duty to remain on PlayStation for now, the long-term impact on platform exclusivity for other IPs remains uncertain.

feed.title: Infographic: what organization of Xbox first-party studios could look like after Activision Blizzard acquisition
feed.summary: An infographic details the potential organizational structure of Xbox first-party studios following the Activision Blizzard acquisition. Microsoft's gaming division would be split into three publishing branches: Xbox Game Studios, Bethesda, and Activision Blizzard, encompassing dozens of in-house studios. The deal, valued at $68.7 billion, is expected to enhance Xbox Game Pass and support Microsoft's metaverse ambitions, although it still requires regulatory and shareholder approval.

feed.title: Will 2022 be the year that SASE comes of age?
feed.summary: The article discusses the evolution and increasing importance of Secure Access Service Edge (SASE) architecture since its inception in 2019. It highlights how SASE, which converges security and WAN infrastructure, is becoming a customer priority, especially for hybrid work environments, due to its ability to secure access to applications from any location and its zero-trust network principles. While SASE is still evolving, companies like Cisco are already offering components of this architecture, leading to measurable threat reduction.

feed.title: How to Build a Multicloud Kubernetes Cluster in AWS and Azure Step by Step
feed.summary: This article provides a step-by-step guide to building a multicloud Kubernetes cluster spanning AWS and Azure. It details the process of configuring a master node on AWS and worker nodes across both AWS and Azure, emphasizing the benefits of multicloud deployments like reduced vendor lock-in and increased resilience. feed.title: SRE: Benefits and Business Impact of the SRE Mindset
feed.summary: This article discusses the benefits and business impact of adopting a Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) mindset. It explains how SRE, originating from Google, offers a concrete model to implement the DevOps philosophy by balancing feature development velocity with operational reliability risks. The SRE model aims to raise operational excellence, foster unified engineering vision, and redefine operations as a value creation center through concepts like SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets.

feed.title: FedEx and Microsoft announce new cross-platform logistics solution for e-commerce
feed.summary: FedEx and Microsoft are expanding their collaboration to introduce a new cross-platform "logistics as a service" solution for retailers, merchants, and brands. This offering will integrate FedEx network intelligence with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Intelligent Order Management to improve customer engagement, shipping options, and supply chain visibility. The initiative aims to help businesses better fulfill, ship, and service customer orders by leveraging AI and machine learning from the vast data generated by FedEx's daily operations.

feed.title: Ministry of the Presidency and Microsoft sign collaboration agreement to improve protection and defense against cyberthreats
feed.summary: The Ministry of the Presidency of the Dominican Republic and Microsoft Corporation have signed a collaboration agreement to enhance protection and defense against cyberthreats. This agreement makes the Dominican Republic the first Caribbean country and the only active Latin American country to join Microsoft's Government Security Program (GSP). The program provides access to Microsoft technology, security information, and facilitates collaboration between Microsoft and government cybersecurity experts.

feed.title: Microsoft to Acquire Activision Blizzard for $68.7B, Becoming Third Largest Gaming Company
feed.summary: Microsoft Corporation is set to acquire Activision Blizzard Inc. in a $68.7 billion cash deal, which will make Microsoft the third-largest gaming company globally. This acquisition will add major game franchises like Warcraft and Call of Duty to Microsoft's portfolio and integrate them into its Game Pass service, significantly expanding its presence in mobile, PC, console, and cloud gaming. The deal is expected to close in fiscal year 2023, pending regulatory approval.

feed.title: Is chip giant Nvidia going to scrap its $40BN bid for Arm?
authors: Giles Turner and Peter Elstrom and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to abandon its $40 billion acquisition of Arm Ltd. due to fierce regulatory backlash and little progress in securing approvals. Regulators and customers, including the U.S. FTC, have expressed concerns that the deal would make Nvidia too powerful. SoftBank, Arm's current owner, is stepping up preparations for an Arm initial public offering as an alternative.

feed.title: Biden Gets CEO Support for Economic Agenda
feed.summary: President Joe Biden met with CEOs from major companies like General Motors, Ford, and Microsoft to garner support for his economic agenda, which includes nearly $2 trillion in spending and tax increases focusing on climate, manufacturing, and child care. Despite the Senate stalling the "Build Back Better" plan, these business leaders, including Cummins CEO Tom Linebarger and GM CEO Mary Barra, expressed support for aspects like child care subsidies and increased semiconductor production. The White House is now exploring which components of the plan can secure the necessary votes in Congress.

feed.title: Data platform modernization delivering richer insights and powering dynamic digital experiences for TD customers
feed.summary: TD Bank Group is accelerating its data platform modernization by establishing an enterprise-level data estate on Microsoft Azure, including a new multi-year agreement with Databricks. This initiative aims to enhance analytical capabilities, power new customer experiences, and enable greater agility across the bank. Leveraging Azure Data Services and Databricks on Azure will facilitate data democratization and provide advanced analytics tools to drive critical business decisions and customer-centric innovation.

feed.title: Wall Street gains evaporate, S&P 500 ends lower on Fed tightening timeline
feed.summary: The S&P 500 ended lower after the U.S. Federal Reserve indicated it would soon raise interest rates to combat persistent inflation. All three major U.S. stock indexes swung wildly, with the Dow and S&P 500 closing in negative territory, while Nasdaq saw a nominal gain. The market reacted strongly to Fed Chair Jerome Powell's comments about inflation and supply problems being more severe and long-lasting than anticipated.

feed.title: DISH Sets Data in Motion with Confluent, Unlocking the Power of the First 5G Smart Network™
feed.summary: DISH Network Corporation is partnering with Confluent to leverage cloud-native data streaming with Apache Kafka for real-time analytics on its new smart 5G network. This collaboration, using AWS infrastructure, aims to create a central network nervous system, enabling DISH to deploy a scalable and elastic data architecture that enhances performance, streamlines dynamic behaviors, and provides game-changing real-time intelligence for DISH and its enterprise customers.

feed.title: Adobe Inc. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
feed.summary: Adobe Inc. (ADBE) stock declined by 1.55% on Thursday, closing at $493.05, amid a general downturn in the stock market where the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also fell. This marks its third consecutive day of losses, leaving the stock $206.49 below its 52-week high. While Adobe underperformed some rivals like Microsoft Corp. and Salesforce.com Inc., it still fared better than SAP SE ADR.

feed.title: Gartner Recommends Organizations Confront Three Internal Labor Market Inequities to Retain Talent
feed.summary: Gartner advises organizations to address three internal labor market inequities to improve employee retention amidst the ongoing "Great Resignation." These inequities—unequal awareness, access, and support—hinder employee agility and fair internal hiring processes. By leveraging technology to democratize awareness, opening access to opportunities, and encouraging manager support for mobility, companies can foster a more equitable environment, leading to higher performance and reduced turnover.

feed.title: Fidelity kickstarts process to list metaverse and crypto company ETFs
feed.summary: Fidelity Investments has initiated the process with the SEC to launch two new exchange-traded funds (ETFs) targeting the crypto and metaverse sectors. The Crypto Industry and Digital Payments ETF will focus on companies involved in crypto mining, blockchain technology, and digital payments, while the Fidelity Metaverse ETF will track companies generating revenue from metaverse-related technologies. This development follows Fidelity's previous attempts to launch crypto-related investment products, including a rejected spot bitcoin ETF in the US and a Canadian Bitcoin ETF.

feed.title: Customer engagement enhanced with cloud-based analytics and AI
feed.summary: 1-800-FLOWERS.COM, Inc. has significantly enhanced its customer engagement and personalized marketing efforts by adopting SAS Viya on Microsoft Azure. This transition allows the e-commerce retailer to leverage cloud-based analytics and AI to understand customer behavior, execute complex marketing campaigns, and rapidly scale operations, especially during peak seasons. The move has also provided increased flexibility for its distributed workforce and enabled continuous improvement through data-driven experimentation.

feed.title: Apple’s $124 Billion Cult of Personality, PLUG-ing Back in & An EV Road Trip
feed.summary: This article discusses Apple's impressive Q4 2021 earnings, highlighting its massive revenue and ability to navigate supply chain issues, despite the author's personal dislike for the company. It also addresses reader questions regarding Plug Power (PLUG) stock's recent performance and the considerations for long EV road trips, emphasizing the current challenges with charging infrastructure compared to gasoline vehicles.

feed.title: Kamal Nath
feed.summary: Kamal Nath, CEO of Sify Technologies, attributes his 2021 CEO of the Year award to his team and the company's entrepreneurial spirit. With nearly 30 years of experience, Nath transformed Sify from a network and data center services company into a comprehensive ICT solutions provider, making it India's leading player in data centers, cloud, and network services. He emphasizes teamwork and a philosophy inspired by football, where every member supports the overall objective beyond their defined roles.

feed.title: SONY PICTURES NETWORKS LAUNCHES SONY KAL in US
feed.summary: Sony Pictures Networks India (SPN), in association with Sony Pictures Television (SPT), has launched Sony KAL Hindi, its first free, ad-supported streaming television (FAST) channel in the US. This new general entertainment channel offers celebrated drama and comedy TV series directly from India, and is now available on SLING TV, LG Channels, and Plex, with plans for additional platforms. The launch aims to provide free access to rich South Asian programming to US audiences, further expanding SPN's content distribution efforts in the region.

feed.title: Reference design offers wireless docking over Wi-Fi 6E for PCs
feed.summary: Synaptics Incorporated has introduced Gemini, a reference design that offers wireless docking over Wi-Fi 6E for PCs, claiming it's the world's first true Wi-Fi 6/6E wireless docking experience for laptops. This technology enables full dual-4K display capability and ultra-low latency, comparable to wired connections, and integrates hardware and software components like the BCM43752 Wi-Fi 6/6E radio and DL-1950 video interface IC. While initially focused on PC docking, Gemini's applications extend to tablets, gaming, and VR, with analyst Patrick Moorhead highlighting its potential to revolutionize connectivity in hybrid work environments.

feed.title: Sony to buy game maker Bungie in $3.6 billion deal.
feed.summary: Sony Interactive Entertainment announced its acquisition of video game developer Bungie for $3.6 billion, following recent major deals by Microsoft and Take-Two Interactive. Bungie, known for Destiny and previously Halo, will operate independently, with Sony aiming to expand PlayStation's reach to a wider audience. This move reunites Bungie with a major console maker after its split from Microsoft in 2007.

feed.title: Sony to Buy ‘Halo,’ ‘Destiny’ Video Game Developer Bungie in $3.6B Deal
feed.summary: Sony has announced its intention to acquire Bungie, the developer behind popular video game franchises like Halo and Destiny, for $3.6 billion. Following the acquisition, Bungie will operate as an independent subsidiary of Sony Interactive Entertainment, maintaining its current management and board. This deal is part of a larger trend of consolidation in the gaming industry, coming after Microsoft's announcement to buy Activision Blizzard and Take-Two Interactive's acquisition of Zynga.

feed.title: Electronic Arts Names Chris Suh as Chief Financial Officer
feed.summary: Electronic Arts Inc. (NASDAQ: EA) announced Chris Suh as its new Chief Financial Officer, effective March 1. Suh, previously Corporate Vice President and CFO of Microsoft's Cloud + AI group, will report to Chairman and CEO Andrew Wilson and oversee various financial functions. He replaces Blake Jorgensen, who is stepping down after nearly a decade.

feed.title: Home Depot launches training program to support construction industry
feed.summary: Home Depot has launched a free job-training program called "Path to Pro" to address the significant labor shortage in the construction industry. The program offers self-paced training focused on basic construction skills, job site safety, and soft skills, aiming to connect qualified candidates with potential employers through its "Path to Pro network." This initiative seeks to rebuild interest in construction careers and fill the labor gap with entry-level workers.

feed.title: The Great Video Game Consolidation Is Just Beginning
feed.summary: Sony Group Corp. is acquiring Bungie Inc., creator of Halo and Destiny, for $3.6 billion, signaling a growing consolidation in the video game industry. This acquisition follows other major deals, such as Microsoft's planned purchase of Activision Blizzard and Take-Two Interactive's deal for Zynga, suggesting a "feeding frenzy" as tech and entertainment companies seek talent for metaverse projects. The article predicts more such mergers to come.

feed.title: Morgan Stanley Sees $8 Trillion Metaverse Market — In China Alone
feed.summary: Morgan Stanley predicts an $8 trillion metaverse market in China alone, replacing the mobile internet with a more "immersive experience." The investment bank acknowledges significant technological and regulatory hurdles for mass adoption, estimating an initial total addressable market of $4 trillion before expanding to $8 trillion as it disrupts offline activities.

feed.title: Amazon and Microsoft led the world in corporate purchases of clean energy in 2021
feed.summary: Amazon and Microsoft were global leaders in corporate clean energy power purchase agreements in 2021, with Amazon holding the top spot for the second consecutive year. Combined, the two tech giants procured 12.4 GW of wind and solar power, contributing significantly to a record-setting year for corporate carbon-free energy deals. Both companies are committed to achieving 100% renewable energy for their operations by 2025, with Microsoft aiming for 24/7 clean energy by 2030.

feed.title: Adobe XD Review
feed.summary: Adobe XD is a powerful and intuitive design software for interactive interface design and prototyping, recognized as an Editors' Choice. It excels due to its seamless integration with other Creative Cloud apps and robust responsive design tools. While Sketch is Mac-only, Adobe XD supports both macOS and Windows, making it a versatile option for UI/UX designers, despite having fewer plug-ins than its competitor.

feed.title: EA Revenue Forecast Misses Estimates After Battlefield Flop
feed.summary: Electronic Arts Inc. announced a revenue and earnings forecast for the current quarter that fell short of analysts' expectations, primarily due to the poor performance of its game Battlefield 2042. Despite continued success with Apex Legends and upcoming Star Wars titles, the game's flop has negatively impacted EA's financial outlook and stock performance. The company also announced Chris Suh as its new chief financial officer.

feed.title: LGD and BOE Competing with SDC for Larger Share of iPhone Business
feed.summary: LG Display (LGD) and BOE are increasing their competition with Samsung Display (SDC) for a larger share of Apple's iPhone OLED panel supply. While Samsung has historically dominated, Apple's strategy to minimize dependency has encouraged LGD and BOE to expand capacity and technology, leading to forecasted shifts in panel supplier percentages for future iPhone models. Chinese display manufacturers like BOE, Visionox, and CSOT are also significantly investing in flexible OLED screens, challenging South Korean dominance and aiming to capture a larger portion of the growing foldable smartphone market.

feed.title: SentinelOne vs Palo Alto Networks
feed.summary: This article compares SentinelOne and Palo Alto Networks, highlighting SentinelOne's advantages in deployment, management, AI capabilities, and cloud security. It positions SentinelOne as a leader in endpoint protection and autonomous cybersecurity, emphasizing its unified platform, real-time protection, and AI-powered solutions, contrasting them with Palo Alto Networks' perceived complexity and disjointed offerings.

feed.title: Equiteq advises Just Analytics on sale to global player Rackspace
feed.summary: Equiteq advised Singapore-based Just Analytics, a firm specializing in advanced analytics, big data, and artificial intelligence, on its sale to global cloud group Rackspace Technology. Just Analytics, founded in 2011, has over 100 professionals across offices in Singapore, Vietnam, and India. The acquisition will allow Rackspace Technology to expand its presence in Asia Pacific and deepen its expertise in the Azure cloud landscape, while Just Analytics will continue to operate under its own brand.

feed.title: Alphabet brings big stock splits back to market
authors: Jeran Wittenstein and Vivianne Rodrigues and Bloomberg
feed.summary: Alphabet Inc. announced a 20-for-1 stock split, aiming to make its shares more accessible to small investors by reducing the per-share price. This move is also seen as a step towards potential inclusion in the Dow Jones Industrial Average, which has historically been a barrier due to Alphabet's high stock price. The announcement led to a 10% jump in shares during premarket trading.

feed.title: Alphabet eyes $2 trillion value after blowout results
feed.summary: Alphabet Inc. is on the verge of joining Apple and Microsoft in the $2 trillion market valuation club after a strong quarterly report led to an over 8% surge in its shares. The company also announced a 20-to-1 stock split, aiming to make shares more accessible to retail investors. At least 20 brokerages raised their price targets on Alphabet's stock.

feed.title: Check Point Software sees up to 10% sales growth in 2022
feed.summary: Check Point Software Technologies exceeded earnings estimates in the fourth quarter and projected a revenue growth of up to 10% for 2022, partly driven by its new Quantum Lightspeed firewall. The company expects revenues between $2.2 billion and $2.375 billion this year, following a 5% increase in 2021. Despite cautious optimism due to supply chain risks and the global economy, Check Point plans increased investments in its workforce, R&D, and other growth drivers.

feed.title: 10 immutable laws of security administration redux
feed.summary: This article revisits Scott Culp's "10 Immutable Laws of Security Administration" 20 years after their initial publication. The author, Brett James, analyzes each law to assess its continued relevance in today's cybersecurity landscape. He concludes that most of the laws remain highly applicable, with some requiring updated technological contexts, and highlights the ongoing importance of vigilance, good administration, and risk management in security.

feed.title: International Funds Stop Fresh Transactions. Is It a Worrying Sign?
feed.summary: Mutual fund investors were surprised when fund houses stopped fresh transactions in schemes offering exposure to offshore equities. This industry-wide decision was prompted by the Indian mutual fund industry reaching its overall investment limit of USD 7 billion in offshore securities, set by the RBI in 2008. While many funds have temporarily suspended inflows into schemes with overseas exposure, certain overseas ETFs may still accept investments as they fall under a separate, unbreached limit.

feed.title: Amazon notches up sunny sales, despite client shift to 'multicloud',
feed.summary: Amazon's cloud computing division, Amazon Web Services (AWS), has continued to show strong sales growth for four consecutive quarters, easing concerns that a move towards "multicloud" strategies by clients would diminish its market share. While some companies are adopting multiple cloud vendors for diversification, major players like AWS, Microsoft Azure, and Google Cloud are still gaining market share from smaller competitors, indicating that even in a multicloud approach, a primary cloud provider often remains dominant. This robust performance underscores significant growth in the wider cloud industry, with overall spending jumping by 37% in 2021.

feed.title: Apple, Broadcom win new trial in $1.1 bln Caltech patent case
feed.summary: A U.S. appeals court has invalidated a $1.1 billion jury verdict against Apple and Broadcom in a patent infringement case brought by the California Institute of Technology (Caltech). The court deemed the damages "legally unsupportable" and ordered a new trial on the amount of damages, while upholding the infringement findings for two of Caltech's patents. The case revolves around Caltech's Wi-Fi technology patents used in millions of Apple devices containing Broadcom chips.

feed.title: Apple, Broadcom Win New Trial In $1.1BN Caltech Patent Case
feed.summary: A United States appeals court has overturned a jury's decision that ordered Apple and Broadcom to pay $1.1 billion to Caltech for infringing on Wi-Fi technology patents, ordering a new trial on damages. The court deemed the original award "legally unsupportable" but upheld the finding of infringement on two patents and called for a new trial on a third. Caltech's two-tier damages model was rejected by the appeals court, which found it legally unsound.

feed.title: Johnson & Johnson leaders discuss what’s possible with the Microsoft cloud deal
feed.summary: Johnson & Johnson (J&J) leaders, Group CIO Larry Jones and Office of Digital Innovation Leader Peter Schulam, discussed their cloud partnership with Microsoft and its potential to transform medical devices and surgical procedures. They emphasized how cloud capabilities can enable smart devices, create new standards of care through data aggregation and AI, and democratize high-quality healthcare. The leaders also highlighted the importance for medical device designers to integrate connectivity and security from the outset, drawing on Microsoft's expertise to innovate more efficiently.

feed.title: Virtusa and Pegasystems at the service of global insurance
feed.summary: Virtusa, a global IT services company, and Pegasystems, a software company, are collaborating to help the insurance industry embrace digital transformation. The article highlights how this partnership assists insurers in adopting hyper-automation, leveraging low-code/no-code DPA platforms, and modernizing legacy systems to improve efficiency and customer experience. Virtusa's unique approach as a digital engineering company, combined with its long-standing relationship with Pega, positions it to address the insurance sector's evolving needs, especially in a post-pandemic landscape requiring seamless digital interactions.

feed.title: Sify Technologies: Simplifies digital adoption
feed.summary: Sify Technologies, led by CEO Kamal Nath, has strategically placed cloud@core at the center of its offerings to simplify digital adoption for businesses. The company, headquartered in Chennai and listed on NASDAQ, has transformed from a consumer-facing entity to an enterprise-focused ICT solutions provider, leveraging its data centers, network, and cloud capabilities. Sify emphasizes partnerships, resilience, and continuous innovation to meet the evolving digital transformation needs of its diverse customer base.

feed.title: Traditional conglomerates such as GE, J&J and Toshiba are moving in a new direction
feed.summary: Traditional conglomerates like General Electric, Johnson & Johnson, and Toshiba are breaking up their companies to increase shareholder value and simplify management. This trend is driven by past financial difficulties and the complexities of their diversified operations. In contrast, modern tech giants like Amazon and Meta thrive as conglomerates by leveraging platform-based models and network effects, which offer a different approach to managing varied businesses.
