feed.summary: The article reviews the UHERO fund, which invests in the growing global gaming industry through the "The Global X Video Games & Esports ETF (HERO)". It details the industry's massive growth, exceeding music and film combined, and outlines UHERO's investment focus on companies like Nvidia, Electronic Arts, NetEase, Blizzard, and Nintendo, primarily in the US, Japan, and Korea. The fund is presented as a high-growth, high-volatility option for investors interested in alternative industries.

feed.title: Opinion: $1.4 trillion? Big Tech’s pandemic year produces mind-boggling financial results
feed.summary: In 2021, despite supply-chain disruptions, labor shortages, and rising prices, major tech companies including Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Microsoft achieved staggering financial results. They collectively saw over $320 billion in profit on $1.4 trillion in sales, with profits increasing more than 55% and sales growing 27% from an already record-setting base. This performance highlights Big Tech's resilience and expanding economic influence, making their combined sales comparable to a top-15 global economy.

feed.title: Amazon hiking base salary cap to $350,000 for corporate, tech workers
feed.summary: Amazon has announced a significant increase in its base salary cap for corporate and tech workers, raising it from $160,000 to $350,000. This move aims to enhance the company's competitiveness in a challenging labor market and attract and retain top talent. The company indicated that these increases are "much more considerable" than in previous years, aligning its pay structure more closely with other major tech firms.

feed.title: PLDT and Microsoft seal partnership for Threat Intelligence sharing to combat rising Cybercrime in the Philippines
feed.summary: PLDT Inc. and Microsoft have formed a strategic partnership through Microsoft's Cyber Threat Intelligence Program (CTIP) to enhance the Philippines' digital security against cyber threats. This collaboration provides PLDT with real-time access to Microsoft DCU's Azure-based cyber threat intelligence, enabling better identification and mitigation of cybercrime. Both companies aim to strengthen cybersecurity capabilities and protect over 70 million mobile and 3.7 million broadband customers in the country.

feed.title: Xerox Acquires Powerland, Expanding IT Services Reach Across Canada
feed.summary: Xerox Holdings Corp. has acquired Canadian IT services company Powerland in an all-cash deal to strengthen its IT services offerings in North America, with the aim of becoming a single provider for SMBs' IT and print needs across the region. Powerland, founded in 1985, will retain its name with the addition of "A Xerox Business Solutions Company" and its approximately 100 employees will join Xerox. This acquisition is part of Xerox's strategy to expand its IT services business, following other recent acquisitions in the space.

feed.title: Kiwibank takes payments onto Azure with ACI Worldwide
feed.summary: Kiwibank has partnered with ACI Worldwide to migrate its payment hub to Microsoft's Azure cloud, aiming to deliver real-time experiences and manage system transformation more efficiently. This move will enable Kiwibank to introduce new products faster and scale to meet customer demands, preparing for New Zealand's retail payment system to operate 365 days a year. The partnership emphasizes improved cash flow management, liquidity, and a more responsive approach to the evolving digital payment market.

feed.title: What Nvidia Can’t Buy, It Can Still Get Through An Arm Partnership
feed.summary: Nvidia's $40 billion acquisition of Arm Holdings from SoftBank Group was terminated due to regulatory scrutiny and market resistance, resulting in a $1.25 billion hit for Nvidia. Despite the failed acquisition, Nvidia, an Arm architecture licensee, plans to release its Arm server chip "Grace" next year and may pursue a joint venture partnership with Arm, allowing it to license its GPU and network chip technologies through Arm's licensing machine. The article suggests that such a partnership could enable many of the benefits Nvidia sought through ownership without the regulatory hurdles.

feed.title: Event-led Engagement Platform, Airmeet, Raises $35M USD Series B From Prosus Ventures, Sistema, Sequoia Capital India, RingCentral Ventures, and Others
feed.summary: Airmeet, an event-led engagement platform, announced it has raised $35M USD in Series B funding from new investors including Prosus Ventures, Sistema Asia Fund, and RingCentral Ventures, alongside existing investors Sequoia Capital India and Accel India. The company has experienced significant growth, scaling its recurring revenue 24X since its Series A investment and enabling 150 million minutes of video streaming in 2021. The funds will be used to expand its global footprint, invest in R&D, and scale its go-to-market functions, with a focus on strategic activities to increase brand visibility in the international market.

feed.title: We should never have sold Arm in the first place, says ALEX BRUMMER
feed.summary: Alex Brummer argues that the 2016 sale of British chip designer Arm Holdings to Japan's Softbank for £23 billion was a "serious betrayal" of British technology. He criticizes former Prime Minister Theresa May's government and Cabinet Secretary Jeremy Heywood for facilitating the deal, which he views as short-sighted given Softbank founder Masayoshi Son's intent to use Arm as a bargaining chip rather than for long-term investment. Brummer suggests that following the collapse of Nvidia's £50 billion bid for Arm, the British government has an opportunity to correct past mistakes and bring Arm back to the UK as a public company.

feed.title: $ARKK, Shopify & Tesla’s PE – What’s Trending on YCharts?
feed.summary: This article highlights the most popular stocks, funds, and economic data pages on YCharts in January 2022, based on pageview data. Key trends included interest in Tesla's PE ratio, Shopify's significant drawdown, and the ARK Innovation ETF's declining performance. It details the most viewed company and fund pages, as well as economic data trends like the S&P 500's P/E ratio.

feed.title: FedEx launches 10th annual Small Business Grant Contest, with biggest prize pool yet
feed.summary: FedEx Corp. has initiated its 10th annual Small Business Grant Contest, offering its largest prize pool to date. The delivery service giant will distribute a collective total of $365,000 to winning small businesses. This widespread initiative aims to support and empower the small business community across the nation.

feed.title: Gartner: A quarter of consumers will use the metaverse daily by 2026
feed.summary: A Gartner report predicts that by 2026, 25% of consumers will spend at least one hour daily in the metaverse for various activities like work, shopping, or entertainment. The report advises organizations against over-investing in single metaverse components due to its early and disconnected stage of adoption but emphasizes the potential for digital currencies and immersive online events. Retailers are already engaging with the metaverse by partnering with platforms like Roblox and filing trademarks for virtual goods, while tech giants like Meta and Microsoft are investing heavily in its development.

feed.title: Sustainability in business practices: What IT should know
feed.summary: This article discusses the increasing importance of sustainability in business practices, focusing on the role of IT. Bjoern Stengel, global sustainability research lead at IDC, highlights how technology enables sustainable transformation, the growing pressure from investors and stakeholders for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) compliance, and the importance of data in achieving greener business practices. He also touches on specific areas like supply chain sustainability and water usage.

feed.title: Samsung, Amdocs collaborate for private 5G at Howard University
feed.summary: Amdocs and Samsung Electronics America have partnered to deploy a Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS)-based private 5G network across Howard University’s campus in Washington D.C. This network aims to enhance digital learning, information access, security, and reliability for over 6,000 students, faculty, and residents. The deployment utilized Samsung RAN technology and Amdocs served as the lead systems integrator, designing and managing the network.

feed.title: Microsoft’s Asenso Pilipinas Summit Gathers Government Leaders to Empower Stronger Digital Organizations across the Philippines – Microsoft News Center Philippines
feed.summary: Microsoft recently held its 5th annual Asenso Pilipinas summit, bringing together nearly 3,000 public officials to discuss navigating change and building stronger digital organizations post-COVID-19. The event focused on empowering governments to engage citizens, modernize workplaces, and enhance services through technology, with keynotes and plenary sessions on hybrid work, hyper-connected government, AI, and end-to-end security. Microsoft also committed to investing $20 billion over five years to accelerate cybersecurity efforts globally.

feed.title: Can A Vintage T. Rowe Price Fund Ride Rivian, Microsoft And Snap To The Moon?
feed.summary: Portfolio manager Joe Fath is revitalizing the T. Rowe Price Growth Stock Fund, founded in 1950, by investing heavily in new tech companies and focusing on "disruptive change," contrasting with the fund's historical picks like IBM. Despite facing outflows to passive management, Fath's strategy involves concentrated bets in private companies like Rivian, and public tech giants such as Microsoft, achieving significant returns. He remains confident in these high-growth, high-volatility investments, believing their long-term growth profiles will ultimately reward shareholders.

feed.title: Knowles Celebrates 75 Years Of Industry Firsts And Leadership In The Audio Industry
feed.summary: Knowles Corporation celebrates 75 years of innovation and leadership in the audio industry, from its founding in 1946 to its current status as a market leader in audio components. The article highlights key milestones such as the development of miniature microphones for hearing aids, the groundbreaking SiSonic MEMS microphones, and balanced armature drivers that have revolutionized both medical and consumer audio. Knowles continues to drive advancements in areas like TWS earphones, voice control, and space exploration, shaping the future of how we interact with sound.

feed.title: Best Load Balancers & Load Balancing Software
feed.summary: This article reviews the best load balancers and load balancing software solutions available, covering a range of types including hardware, software, cloud, and virtual appliances. It details offerings from major vendors like A10 Networks, AWS, Citrix, F5, HAProxy, and VMware, comparing their features, pros, and cons. The piece also explains what load balancing is, how it works, different load balancing algorithms, and what application delivery controllers (ADCs) are, helping readers choose the right solution for their IT infrastructure.

feed.title: Jobs in Hyderabad: Microsoft invites applications from freshers
feed.summary: Microsoft is inviting applications from freshers for engineering jobs in its Hyderabad office. Eligible candidates must have a B.Tech, M.Tech, or MS degree in Computer Science or a related field with a minimum CGPA of 7.5/10 and be from the 2022 batch. Selected candidates may work in Hyderabad, Bangalore, or Noida, with responsibilities including planning, design, and implementation.

feed.title: IoT and Saas-built AgriTech for Smart Farming
feed.summary: This article features an interview with Kunal Tiwari of Digital Green, discussing the transformative role of technology like IoT, SaaS, AI, and ML in modern agriculture, particularly in India. It highlights how these technologies are enabling "smart farming" and "precision farming" to increase productivity, improve farmers' income, and make agriculture more sustainable. Tiwari explains Digital Green's strategy for empowering smallholder farmers through technology-enabled communication and partnerships.

feed.title: Cisco Has Discussed Deal for Software Company Splunk (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Cisco Systems has held discussions with the software company Splunk about a potential acquisition, though no deal is currently solid. If talks resume, Cisco could acquire Splunk for over $20 billion, significantly higher than Splunk's current market capitalization of around $18 billion. This potential acquisition aligns with Cisco's strategy of growth through mergers and acquisitions, particularly in the security sector.

feed.title: Microsoft to potentially give up 30% commission on Xbox in wake of regulatory pressure
feed.summary: Microsoft is considering revising its standard 30% commission on Xbox to a more flexible model due to increasing regulatory pressure, especially ahead of the Activision Blizzard acquisition. While the company has committed to several "open app store" principles for its PC store and some for Xbox, it still justifies the 30% cut by selling consoles at a loss. Microsoft states it aims to evolve its business model to center on players and adaptability to regulation, though concrete changes are not yet fully promised for Xbox.

feed.title: Microsoft announces plan to fully reopen corporate offices in Redmond, elsewhere
feed.summary: Microsoft is planning to fully reopen its corporate campuses in Redmond and elsewhere by February 28, moving to the final stage of its hybrid work plan. This decision comes as COVID-19 cases from the omicron variant are waning and local vaccination rates are high, allowing for the return of employees, visitors, and guests. While facilities will fully open, the company will continue to allow some form of remote work and offer scheduling flexibility for many workers.

feed.title: What is ServiceNow Impact? An app to keep digital transformations on track
feed.summary: ServiceNow has introduced "Impact," a new app designed to help customers maximize the value derived from their ServiceNow subscriptions and bridge the "value gap" in digital transformation investments. Available in four tiers, including a free "Base" level and three paid tiers offering increasing levels of support and features, Impact aims to encourage broader consumption of ServiceNow's products by providing tools for measuring progress, personalized training, and developer support. While presented as a product rather than a service, customer renewal of Impact will depend on its ability to deliver expected value.

feed.title: Oracle adds support for the MongoDB API, makes its case for value of the converged database
feed.summary: Oracle has announced support for the MongoDB API, allowing enterprises to run MongoDB data applications on Oracle Autonomous Database without retooling their MongoDB environment. This move, highlighted by Oracle's Gerald Venzl, signifies a continuation of the converged database strategy, enabling users to leverage both SQL and NoSQL functionalities within a single cloud service. Oracle believes this offers a distinct advantage over competitors by providing a full array of data models and analytics capabilities without requiring multiple services.

feed.title: Microsoft tells workers to prepare to return to the office. (Published 2022)
feed.summary: Microsoft has informed its employees that they will need to return to the office starting on February 28, transitioning back to a corporate campus environment for the first time since the Omicron variant. The company plans for a hybrid work model, allowing most employees to work from home up to 50 percent of the time. This decision is based on high vaccination rates and declining hospitalization and death rates in King County, where Microsoft's headquarters are located.

feed.title: NERD ETF gains from strong demand for esports
feed.summary: The Roundhill BITKRAFT Esports and Digital Entertainment ETF (NERD) has seen its share price rise due to sustained interest in esports and video games, as well as the excitement surrounding Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard. Despite a tough period over the last year, the ETF is benefiting from increased M&A activity in the gaming industry and strong demand figures for esports viewership and video game sales. The ETF's future growth is expected to be driven by continued demand, monetization model evolution including blockchain and NFTs, virtual reality, and cloud gaming.

feed.title: Perion Network wins Microsoft Advertising award
feed.summary: Perion Network has won a Microsoft Advertising award, gaining recognition for its work in the advertising technology sector. This achievement was highlighted in an article published in The Jerusalem Post. The company's success points to its advancements and contributions within the high-tech and business innovation landscape.

feed.title: Akamai pays $900M to acquire AWS cloud infrastructure rival Linode
feed.summary: Akamai Technologies Inc. has announced its acquisition of Linode LLC for approximately $900 million. This strategic move aims to transform Akamai into a highly distributed compute platform, enhancing its offerings for developers by combining Linode's cloud computing capabilities with Akamai's edge platform and security tools. The acquisition follows Akamai's strong fourth-quarter financial results and is expected to add about $100 million in revenue by year-end.

feed.title: Gartner Magic Quadrant for Data and Analytics Service Providers 2022
feed.summary: Gartner has released its 2022 Magic Quadrant report for Data and Analytics Service Providers, evaluating 18 global providers and identifying 12 market leaders. The report categorizes vendors into Leaders, Challengers, Visionaries, and Niche Players based on their completeness of vision and ability to execute. Leaders include Accenture, Deloitte, and IBM, while Challengers such as NTT DATA and Genpact demonstrate strong execution but perhaps less disruptive vision.

feed.title: JPMorgan Chase spent $2 billion on brand new data centers last year
feed.summary: JPMorgan Chase invested $2 billion in new data centers last year, even while actively migrating data and applications to public cloud platforms like AWS, Google, and Microsoft. This investment is part of their broader annual technology spending, which exceeded $12 billion, focusing on cloud capabilities, digital consumer experience, and data analytics. CEO Jamie Dimon emphasized that the new data centers incorporate "cloud capability," and the firm plans to move 30% to 50% of its applications to the cloud this year, driven by the significant value seen in risk management, fraud prevention, and customer satisfaction.

feed.title: Oracle cloud authorized to host top secret data for DOD
feed.summary: Oracle's cloud technology has received authorization to host top secret and highly sensitive data for the Department of Defense, specifically for the Air Force. The company built special "National Security Regions" to secure this sensitive information. This accreditation positions Oracle alongside Microsoft and Amazon Web Services, which have also been cleared for similar highly sensitive data hosting.

feed.title: Oracle cloud authorized to host top secret data for DOD
feed.summary: Oracle has received authorization to host top secret and sensitive compartmentalized information (TS/SCI) and special access program data for the Department of Defense, specifically the Air Force. The company achieved an Authority to Operate (ATO) for its "National Security Regions" which are designed with robust security features. This accreditation allows Oracle to process some of the Air Force's most sensitive data, joining other major cloud providers like Microsoft and Amazon Web Services in this capability.

feed.title: Trip.com To Launch Hybrid Work In Chinese Tech Sector First
feed.summary: Trip.com Group is set to become the first major Chinese tech company to implement a hybrid work model, allowing employees to work remotely two days a week starting March 1st. Executive Chairman James Liang stated that a six-month trial showed a one-third reduction in staff turnover and improved efficiency without a significant impact on performance. This move aims to boost morale and challenge the prevalent "996" overwork culture in China's tech sector.

feed.title: F5 Strengthens Protection of the Digital World with F5 Distributed Cloud Services
feed.summary: F5 announced a significant expansion of its application security and delivery portfolio with F5 Distributed Cloud Services, a unified SaaS platform offering security, multi-cloud networking, and edge-based computing solutions. The company also launched F5 Distributed Cloud WAAP, integrating various security capabilities into one SaaS offering to simplify security management for modern and legacy applications across diverse environments. This move addresses the increasing complexity and threats faced by organizations operating multi-cloud and hybrid application architectures.

feed.title: Oracle gets go-ahead to host top secret Air Force data
feed.summary: Oracle has received authorization to host top-secret U.S. Air Force data on its National Security Regions cloud platforms. This expands Oracle's role in the military sector, allowing it to handle highly sensitive information for the Department of Defense. The company has a history of government contracts, including involvement with the Air Force's Advanced Battle Management System and the CIA's Commercial Cloud Enterprise.

feed.title: How to Not Stress About Tech
feed.summary: The article discusses how investors can avoid stressing over the tech sector's current volatility by being selective and focusing on quality companies. It highlights the Goldman Sachs Innovate Equity ETF (GINN) as an example of a fund that invests in profitable, cash-generating tech firms with strong competitive advantages, distinguishing them from “pandemic losers.” The piece emphasizes that while some pandemic-driven tech trends are fading, long-term secular growth themes persist, making selective tech investments still attractive.

feed.title: SPYG, VOOG, And IVW: It's Gut Check Time For Owners Of These S&P 500 Growth Funds
feed.summary: This article examines three S&P 500 Growth Index ETFs: SPYG, VOOG, and IVW, highlighting their strong past performance and heavy concentration in mega-cap stocks. It suggests that while these funds are solid long-term choices, current market conditions, including a downward trend in earnings surprises, might present a better entry point in the future. The author also suggests considering the Invesco S&P 500 Pure Growth ETF for a different approach.

feed.title: Corporate Leadership Won’t Reach Gender Parity Until 2060 at Its Current Rate
feed.summary: A Morningstar analysis indicates that at the current rate of progress, women will not achieve representation parity in corporate leadership until 2060. The study found that the gender pay gap in the C-suite widened in 2020, reversing previous improvements, with women earning significantly less than men, particularly in share-based compensation. This persistent gap highlights institutional barriers despite some incremental increases in female representation at the executive level.

feed.title: How to Let Go of Stress About Tech
feed.summary: The technology sector has had a rough start to the year, but investors shouldn't abandon it. Rather than stressing over technology stocks, investors can embrace quality names over speculative ones through exchange traded funds like the Goldman Sachs Innovate Equity ETF (GINN). GINN focuses on profitable, cash-generating companies with wide competitive moats, such as Apple, Microsoft, and Nvidia, which are expected to perform better as pandemic-related growth tails fade.

feed.title: Build your knowledge of Azure AD conditional access policies
feed.summary: This article explains how Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) conditional access policies help IT control access to resources in a dynamic, cloud-heavy environment. It details how these policies use signals and real-time risk intelligence to grant, restrict, or deny access, building a layered security approach. The article also covers the configuration of conditional access policies, including setting conditions based on user risk, sign-in risk, device platforms, and location, and how to filter access to privileged resources.

feed.title: Inside Pat Gelsinger’s audacious $43.5B plan to revive Intel
feed.summary: This article details Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger's plans to revitalize the company, which has recently faced significant challenges from competitors like Apple and AMD, and struggled with manufacturing delays. Gelsinger, who rejoined Intel after a period away, aims to tackle both technological and cultural issues to restore Intel's preeminence in the chip industry. His experience at Intel during its heyday positions him to address these intricate problems, including a new business model centered on investing $43.5 billion to regain its manufacturing edge.

feed.title: Actual, which renders company ESG data in a SimCity-like platform, raises $5M seed
feed.summary: Actual, a San Francisco-based startup, has secured $5 million in seed funding for its SimCity-like platform that visualizes and helps manage Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) data for companies. Founded by alums from LinkedIn and Airbus, the platform aims to assist businesses in modeling and executing their ESG plans to meet regulations and investor expectations. Actual's "model first" approach allows companies to use existing data, even low-resolution, to forecast future scenarios and transformations.

feed.title: JPMorgan Chase, Toshiba and Ciena Build the First Quantum Key Distribution Network Used to Secure Mission-Critical Blockchain Application
feed.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Toshiba, and Ciena have successfully built and demonstrated the first quantum key distribution (QKD) network for metropolitan areas, securing a mission-critical blockchain application. This groundbreaking research proves the viability of QKD to detect and defend against potential quantum computing attacks, supporting 800 Gbps data rates under real-world conditions. The network secured Liink by J.P. Morgan, the world's first bank-led, production-grade, peer-to-peer blockchain network, showcasing the technology's effectiveness against future quantum threats.

feed.title: Insight Names Alexander L. Baum as Board Director
feed.summary: Insight Enterprises has appointed Alexander L. Baum, a partner at ValueAct Capital and a significant investor in the company, as an independent director to its board. This addition aims to leverage Baum's extensive experience in IT industry strategy and investment expertise to further Insight's transformation into a leading solutions integrator. ValueAct Capital expresses excitement about deepening its relationship with Insight, believing its transformation in response to the changing IT landscape is underappreciated.

feed.title: How the 'Big Short DAO' Bet Against the Crypto Market and Won
feed.summary: The pseudonymous crypto trader @GiganticRebirth, also known as GCR, successfully bet against the crypto market's altcoins after sensing bearish sentiment at the market's peak in November. He assembled a team known as RebirthDAO to research tokenomics and market conditions, leading to profitable short positions on various altcoins. GCR's conviction was based on market exuberance, seasonal trends, and the inflationary nature of certain altcoins due to their unlock schedules.

feed.title: After delaying over crime concerns, Weyerhaeuser says workers will return to downtown Seattle office
feed.summary: Weyerhaeuser is set to reopen its Pioneer Square headquarters in April 2022, after delaying reopening efforts last fall due to concerns about street crime in downtown Seattle. The timber company will implement a hybrid work schedule for employees. This move follows similar announcements from Microsoft and Expedia, signaling a broader return to office for Seattle-based companies.

feed.title: IBM exec referred to older workers as ‘dinobabies,’ suit says
feed.summary: A lawsuit against IBM has revealed email communications where a high-level executive referred to older workers as "dinobabies" and expressed intent to usher them out to "accelerate change." The suit claims IBM had a "top-down plan to retain younger workers" to improve its demographic makeup. This incident highlights ongoing ageism concerns within IBM and the broader tech industry.

feed.title: What’s Changed: 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Information Archiving
feed.summary: The article analyzes the 2022 Gartner Magic Quadrant for Enterprise Information Archiving, highlighting the evolving market driven by digital communication and application data. It discusses changes in vendor inclusion criteria, significant movements of key players like Global Relay and Veritas Technologies into the Leaders quadrant, and the strengths of various providers across the Leaders, Visionaries, and Niche Players categories, including Microsoft, Smarsh, Proofpoint, Mimecast, Micro Focus, ZL, Archive360, Solix Technologies, Barracuda, and Jatheon.

feed.title: PE Firm Capficiency Acquires Microsoft SharePoint Partner KWizCom Corporation -
feed.summary: Private equity firm Capficiency has acquired KWizCom Corporation, a Microsoft SharePoint applications developer, for an undisclosed sum. This acquisition expands Capficiency’s portfolio of IT companies, which also includes Appficiency, and aims to enhance their ability to provide innovative technology solutions to clients. Capficiency plans to continue pursuing merger, acquisition, and alliance opportunities to bolster the capabilities of both Appficiency and KWizCom.

feed.title: How the Internet of Things is revolutionising the packaging industry
feed.summary: The Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming the packaging industry by enabling companies to move from reactive to predictive operations, particularly in achieving sustainability goals. GlobalData research highlights companies like Tetra Pak, Amcor, and Berry Global as leaders in implementing IoT to enhance efficiency and meet ESG targets. IoT, supported by technologies like 5G and AI, allows for smart decisions, automated processes, and significant cost savings, with global IoT revenue in manufacturing expected to reach $91 billion by 2025.

feed.title: Timing: What Enterprises can learn from the Sports industry
feed.summary: This article explores how the precision timing technologies used in the sports industry, such as RFID and high-speed cameras, can offer valuable lessons for enterprises. It highlights the evolution of timing technology in sports, from early photo-finishes to modern-day microsecond accuracy, emphasizing how these advancements build credibility and ensure fairness. The article then suggests practical applications of these technologies for businesses in various sectors, including toll collection, manufacturing, and event management, to improve operational speed, efficiency, and data collection.

feed.title: Russia Ukraine Cyber Activity: Protect Against Related Cyberthreats
feed.summary: This article details the escalation of Russia-Ukraine cyber activity, focusing on various threats like DDoS attacks, HermeticWiper malware, website defacement, phishing, and scam campaigns. It provides actionable recommendations for organizations to protect themselves, including patching critical software, preparing for ransomware/data destruction, and locking down networks. Palo Alto Networks describes how its products and Unit 42 services can help mitigate these evolving cyberthreats.

feed.title: Why you shouldn’t schedule that next meeting
feed.summary: The article discusses how virtual meetings, which became prevalent during the pandemic, have led to "Zoom fatigue" and decreased productivity due to an excessive focus on meetings over actual work. Experts suggest that businesses should re-evaluate the necessity and format of meetings, advocating for more thoughtful scheduling and leveraging technology for asynchronous collaboration to improve efficiency in the hybrid workplace. The goal is to be intentional about meeting objectives and explore alternatives like emails or chat platforms to ensure productive engagement.

feed.title: Accelerating Innovation Across the Portfolio: Blackstone Collaborates with Microsoft
feed.summary: Blackstone's Portfolio Operations team is collaborating with Microsoft to accelerate digital transformation and improve operating performance across its portfolio companies. By leveraging Microsoft Cloud technologies, portfolio companies can standardize digital capabilities, integrate data for analytics, and accelerate innovation, as exemplified by Merlin Entertainments' rapid adoption of an Azure-based data lake. This strategic alliance aims to drive growth and create value through tailored industry solutions and enhanced digital infrastructure.

feed.title: Salesforce employees revolt over NFT moves
feed.summary: Hundreds of Salesforce employees have revolted against the company's planned move into the NFT market, citing environmental and economic concerns. An open letter signed by over 400 workers addresses cofounder Marc Benioff and co-CEO Bret Taylor, raising issues about the high carbon footprint of blockchain technology and the speculative nature of NFTs. This internal backlash comes shortly after Salesforce highlighted its sustainability efforts, creating a perceived conflict between its stated values and its explorations in the NFT space.

feed.title: Snack Giant Mondelēz International Moves Global Operations onto All-Digital Workspace with Orange Business Services
feed.summary: Mondelēz International is transforming its global operations with an all-digital communications platform based on Microsoft Teams, managed by Orange Business Services. This initiative will unify communication and collaboration for 80,000 employees across 80 countries, eliminating legacy PBX systems and optimizing costs. Orange Business Services will also integrate advanced analytics and A.I. to enhance customer experience, personalize employee service, and provide comprehensive oversight of Mondelēz's operations.

feed.title: Mixed reality helps GE Healthcare train engineers to service complex equipment
feed.summary: GE Healthcare, in collaboration with Microsoft MRPP partner Adjacentech Corporation, has developed a mixed-reality training system using HoloLens 2. This system aims to improve training efficiency and knowledge retention for engineers servicing complex medical equipment like CT and MRI scanners in China. By overlaying holographic 3D visualizations onto real-world objects, the solution provides accurate step-by-step guidance, reducing training time and the risk of equipment damage.

feed.title: What Microsoft's Acquisition of Activision Blizzard Means For Its Gaming Future
feed.summary: Microsoft's acquisition of Activision Blizzard for $68.7 billion is poised to significantly strengthen its position in the gaming industry. The deal grants Microsoft a massive boost in mobile gaming through Activision's King subsidiary and enhances its console gaming library with popular titles like Call of Duty and Diablo. It is also expected to propel the growth of Xbox Game Pass by integrating Activision Blizzard's extensive catalog, attracting its 400 million monthly active players.

feed.title: U.S. Bank Partners With Microsoft to Accelerate the Future of Banking With Cloud Computing
feed.summary: U.S. Bank has announced a significant partnership with Microsoft, selecting Microsoft Azure as its primary cloud provider to modernize its technology foundation. This move aims to accelerate innovation, improve data analysis, and quickly scale new banking products and services for customers and partners. The transition is expected to enhance security, customer privacy, and strengthen technology risk management, while also improving the bank's ability to offer personalized digital experiences.

feed.title: TikTok Star Corporate Natalie Wants You to Know a Few Things About Gen Z
feed.summary: TikTok star Corporate Natalie provides business leaders with insights on how to support Gen Z in the workplace. She highlights the struggles of young workers adapting to hybrid work environments and offers advice on networking, empathy, leveraging side hustles for skill development, and fostering vulnerability. The article emphasizes the unique challenges faced by Gen Z in a post-pandemic work world and how leaders can address them.

feed.title: Warner Music and BlackRock Invest $750 Million in Influence Media, Female-Led Music-Rights Firm
feed.summary: Warner Music Group and BlackRock have jointly invested $750 million in Influence Media, a female-led music-rights firm. This partnership aims to acquire music-rights catalogs from female and diverse artists, focusing on newer, active catalogs rather than established older artists. Influence Media, founded by Lylette Pizarro and Lynn Hazan, plans to work with artists who will retain a stake in their work, and has already invested $300 million in 20 catalogs, including that of songwriter-producer Tainy and hitmaking team The Stereotypes.

feed.title: What you can learn from one co-op’s ransomware attack
feed.summary: Crystal Valley Cooperative, a Minnesota-based agricultural co-op, fell victim to a ransomware attack in September 2021, believed to be perpetrated by a Russian-speaking criminal group. The attack encrypted their files, rendering systems inaccessible for weeks and causing significant logistical challenges during harvest, forcing manual operations and leading to substantial costs for recovery and enhanced security measures. The co-op's experience highlights the importance of robust cybersecurity, even for smaller entities, and the broad impact of such attacks beyond just ransom payments.

feed.title: Hoonigan Brings the Halo Infinite Warthog to Life with 1,000+ Horsepower and Twin Garrett Turbos
feed.summary: Hoonigan, in partnership with Microsoft, has successfully recreated the Halo Infinite Warthog, transforming the fictional vehicle into a real-life beast with over 1,000 horsepower. The build features a custom V8 engine enhanced with twin Garrett GTX3576R Gen II turbochargers, all-wheel drive, and specialized off-road suspension. This engineering feat aimed to meet demanding specifications, including high-speed capability and extreme off-road performance, proving the Warthog's formidable power on the dyno.

feed.title: AT&T Private 5G Edge to Make Private 5G Networks Smarter, Simpler, and More Flexible for Businesses, Schools, and Other Organizations
feed.summary: AT&T is launching "AT&T Private 5G Edge," a new service developed in collaboration with Microsoft, aimed at making private 4G/5G networks simpler and more flexible for various organizations. This integrated platform will provide connectivity and applications with low-latency services at the edge, including the capability to roam onto AT&T's public network. The service leverages Azure private MEC and is designed to support use cases across manufacturing, automotive, and healthcare, allowing for easier adoption and scalability of private cellular networks.

feed.title: U.S. Bank to keep Chaska data center open after move to cloud
feed.summary: U.S. Bank announced its adoption of Microsoft’s Azure for cloud services to run its applications, signaling a shift to a cloud-first approach. Despite this move, the bank plans to keep its data center in Chaska operational. This strategy marks a significant change from their past investments in data centers.

feed.title: How DBMS is Used by Hulu, JPMorgan Chase, and The Weather Company
feed.summary: This article examines how Database Management Systems (DBMS) are crucial for organizations to efficiently store, retrieve, and manage data. It provides case studies of how major companies like Hulu, JPMorgan Chase, and The Weather Company leverage DBMS to address challenges, optimize operations, and maintain data integrity and security, highlighting the benefits over traditional file systems. The article demonstrates the real-world applications and positive outcomes of integrating DBMS in various industries.

feed.title: Global X Launches Dow 30 Covered Call ETF
feed.summary: Global X has launched a new ETF, the Global X Dow 30 Covered Call ETF (DJIA), aimed at generating income through covered call writing around the Dow Jones Industrial Average. This ETF, listed on the NYSE with a 60 basis point expense ratio, is designed to track the DJIA Cboe BuyWrite v2 Index. It will make monthly distributions and save investors the effort of individually executing a covered call strategy.

feed.title: Capital Group Dividend Value ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:CGDV)
feed.summary: The Capital Group Dividend Value ETF (CGDV) is an actively managed exchange-traded fund that primarily invests in dividend-paying, large and mid-cap US companies, aiming to produce income exceeding the average yield on US stocks. Launched on Feb 22, 2022, CGDV has assets under management of $35.92 billion and a current dividend yield of 1.14%. The ETF has seen a 12.3% increase in its stock price this year and its top holdings include NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Broadcom.

feed.title: CRM giant Salesforce acquiring B.C.’s Traction on Demand
feed.summary: Salesforce.com Inc. is acquiring B.C.-based software firm Traction on Demand, which specializes in implementing marketing strategies using Salesforce's CRM services. The Burnaby-based company employs about 500 workers across British Columbia, and its founder had previously resisted selling the company. This acquisition follows Salesforce's recent spree of purchases, including Mobify and Slack Technologies Inc.

feed.title: Duos Technologies helping make railroad industry safer
feed.summary: Duos Technologies, based in Jacksonville, is enhancing railroad safety through the development of a rail car inspection portal that uses cameras and artificial intelligence. These portals allow cameras to inspect rail cars moving at high speeds from numerous angles, generating safety reports that help mechanical carmen perform their jobs more efficiently and safely from a computer screen. The company, founded in 2001, aims to convince the historically traditional railroad industry to adopt this new technology, projecting significant revenue growth for 2022.

feed.title: U.S. Bank partners Microsoft for cloud banking tech upgrade
feed.summary: U.S. Bank has partnered with Microsoft, selecting Microsoft Azure as its primary cloud provider to modernize its technology infrastructure. This collaboration aims to provide the bank with greater flexibility, faster data access and analysis, and accelerated product development, leveraging AI and machine learning while ensuring customer privacy and security. Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella emphasized the growing need for financial institutions to build digital capabilities to meet evolving customer demands.

feed.title: Electrolux
feed.summary: Electrolux, a century-old innovator in home appliances, has implemented IBM's AI-driven operations (AIOps) solutions to automate its global IT infrastructure, significantly reducing IT issue resolution times and improving overall efficiency. This adoption of AIOps, particularly IBM Cloud Pak for Watson AIOps, allows Electrolux to streamline event correlation, enhance expertise within its IT teams, and contribute to its ambitious environmental sustainability goals, including achieving net-zero carbon emissions by 2050. The initiative has shown benefits ranging from faster problem-solving and cost savings to supporting remote work and integrating with manufacturing operations for improved efficiency and resilience.

feed.title: How CFOs can supercharge their organization’s sales forecasting
feed.summary: CFOs face a significant challenge in accurately forecasting sales, as traditional methods are often manual, time-consuming, and prone to becoming outdated quickly. The article introduces the "virtual sales forecast" (VSF) as a modern solution that leverages analytical tools, data connections, and automation to provide more accurate, granular, and frequently updated sales projections. By implementing a VSF, organizations can empower various departments with real-time insights, leading to better strategic planning and operational efficiency.

feed.title: General Dynamics IT President Amy Gilliland Named to 2022 Wash100 Award for Leadership in Cloud Modernization and Cybersecurity Services
feed.summary: Amy Gilliland, president of General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT), has been named a 2022 Wash100 Award recipient for her leadership in cloud modernization and cybersecurity services. This marks her fifth consecutive inclusion on the annual list, recognizing her influence and ability to maintain GDIT's stability and growth. Under her leadership, GDIT secured significant contracts, including a $4.5 billion agreement with the National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency and a $190 million contract to migrate the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office's IT infrastructure to the cloud.

feed.title: Amazon, General Mills, IBM, Microsoft, and Nestle Join 150+ Major U.S. Companies To Oppose Anti-Transgender Legislation in Iowa
feed.summary: Over 150 major U.S. companies, including Amazon, General Mills, IBM, Microsoft, and Nestle, have publicly opposed anti-LGBTQ+ legislation across the country, particularly targeting transgender youth. Business leaders emphasize that such discriminatory laws negatively impact recruitment, retention, and overall business operations, making it difficult to attract and keep talent. The Human Rights Campaign and Freedom for All Americans highlight that these policies harm employees, customers, and communities, urging lawmakers to abandon discriminatory efforts.

feed.title: Samsung Joins Forces with Industry Leaders to Advance 5G vRAN Ecosystem
feed.summary: Samsung has partnered with Dell, HPE, Intel, Red Hat, and Wind River to advance the 5G virtualized RAN (vRAN) ecosystem. This collaboration aims to drive innovation and multiparty efforts for more scalable, flexible, and reliable software-based networks. Samsung, a leader in fully-virtualized 5G RAN, seeks to move vRAN and Open RAN beyond lab tests to major commercial markets with this new ecosystem.

feed.title: Lockheed and Microsoft collaborating on 5G military tech
feed.summary: Lockheed Martin and Microsoft are collaborating to enhance U.S. military communications by integrating Lockheed's hybrid base station technology with Microsoft's Azure cloud services for 5G military applications. This partnership aims to deliver mission-critical solutions at the tactical edge, with successful demonstrations already conducted at Lockheed Martin Space’s 5G test range in Colorado. The initiative, named 5G.MIL, seeks to leverage commercial 5G advancements for military use, building on Lockheed's previous efforts and a recent DoD contract for a 5G testbed.

feed.title: KYNDRYL REPORTS FOURTH QUARTER AND FULL-YEAR 2021 RESULTS
feed.summary: Kyndryl Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: KD) reported its fourth-quarter and full-year 2021 financial results, with full-year revenues totaling $18.7 billion and a net loss of $2.3 billion. The company is strategically positioning itself for growth through new partnerships with cloud hyperscalers and key initiatives focused on increasing signings, transforming service delivery, and addressing substandard margins. Kyndryl also announced significant strategic partnerships with major cloud providers and an expanded customer base following its spin-off from IBM.

feed.title: Arista Networks Inc. stock underperforms Monday when compared to competitors
feed.summary: Arista Networks Inc. (ANET) stock declined by 0.62% to $122.73 on Monday, underperforming the broader market. Despite a previous two-day winning streak, the stock closed below its 52-week high and fared worse than some competitors like Microsoft Corp. (MSFT), which saw a gain. Trading volume was also below its 50-day average.

feed.title: Adobe named a Leader for fifth consecutive year in 2022 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Digital Experience Platforms
feed.summary: Adobe has been recognized as a Leader for the fifth consecutive year in the 2022 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Digital Experience Platforms, positioned highest and furthest to the right for both Ability to Execute and Completeness of Vision. The company highlights its market-leading technology in integrated insights, AI/ML (Adobe Sensei), content management, scale and breadth (handling 21.5 trillion segment evaluations daily), real-time personalization, and the foundational Adobe Experience Platform. Adobe emphasizes its commitment to helping businesses deliver personalized customer experiences at scale, highlighting trust, data privacy, and efficient workflow management with Adobe Workfront as critical components for success.

feed.title: Seagate Technology Holdings PLC stock falls Monday, underperforms market
feed.summary: Seagate Technology Holdings PLC (STX) shares fell 1.66% on Monday, closing at $103.16. This decline occurred during a generally grim trading session for the stock market, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also experiencing drops. The stock traded below its 52-week high and showed mixed performance compared to competitors like Microsoft Corp. (MSFT), HP Inc. (HPQ), and Western Digital Corp. (WDC).

feed.title: Accenture and Microsoft to Assist Mount Sinai Health System on Five-Year Transformation Journey to Cloud
feed.summary: Accenture and Microsoft are partnering with Mount Sinai Health System for a five-year cloud transformation journey, migrating its clinical applications, including Epic electronic health records, to Microsoft Azure. This strategic move aims to accelerate innovation, enhance patient engagement, and achieve operational efficiencies by allowing Mount Sinai to reinvest cost-savings into its healthcare mission. Accenture will provide managed services post-migration, while Microsoft will ensure quality assurance during the Azure transition.

feed.title: Check Point releases 2022 Cloud Security Report
feed.summary: Check Point Software Technologies Ltd. has released its 2022 Cloud Security Report, highlighting the challenges organizations face in securing cloud infrastructures amidst increasing cloud adoption, a cyber-skills shortage, and a rise in cloud security incidents, primarily due to misconfigurations. The report suggests a growing preference for independent cloud security solutions over cloud vendor security to streamline management across multi-cloud environments. TJ Gonen, VP of Cloud Security at Check Point, emphasizes the need for integrated third-party solutions with unified dashboards to simplify cloud security, reduce misconfiguration risks, and support application development in the cloud.

feed.title: Microsoft Corp Chief Satya Nadella’s son passes away
feed.summary: Zain Nadella, the 26-year-old son of Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and his wife Anu, passed away on Monday morning. Born with cerebral palsy, Zain's journey profoundly influenced Satya Nadella's focus on designing accessible products at Microsoft. The Children's Hospital, where Zain received treatment, collaborated with the Nadella family to establish the Zain Nadella Endowed Chair in Pediatric Neurosciences.

feed.title: Leveraging Technology to Improve The Lives of P&G Consumers
feed.summary: P&G utilizes advanced data-processing technologies like machine learning and artificial intelligence to enhance its products, understand consumer behavior, and streamline operations. This technology-driven approach, which began over five years ago, impacts everything from product development and quality control to personalized consumer communication and supply chain logistics. P&G's strategy focuses on connecting data, facilitating data scientists' work, and developing talent to continuously improve products and consumer experiences.

feed.title: Leaders in Semiconductors, Packaging, IP Suppliers, Foundries, and Cloud Service Providers Join Forces to Standardize Chiplet Ecosystem
feed.summary: A consortium of leading technology companies, including ASE, AMD, Arm, Google Cloud, Intel, Meta, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, and TSMC, has formed to standardize the chiplet ecosystem. They have ratified the Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) 1.0 specification, an open industry standard for die-to-die interconnects, aiming to enable multi-vendor compatibility for System-on-Chip construction. The consortium is open for membership and plans to develop future generations of the UCIe technology.

feed.title: EA, Oracle Among Companies Heeding Ukraine Plea to Stop Business in Russia
feed.summary: Ukraine has requested that approximately 50 tech companies, including Oracle and EA, cease operations in Russia to isolate the country and pressure its government following military action. In response, Oracle announced the suspension of all operations in the Russian Federation, and EA Sports committed to removing Russian national and club teams from its FIFA games. Other major companies like Spotify, Twitter, Meta, Microsoft, and Google have also taken steps to restrict Russian state media or suspend services in Russia.

feed.title: Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group combines AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, TSMC and more
feed.summary: The Universal Chiplet Interconnect Express (UCIe) group, formed by major tech companies like AMD, Arm, Google, Intel, and TSMC, has established a new industry consortium. Their goal is to standardize die-to-die interconnect guidelines and foster an open chiplet ecosystem, developing the UCIe 1.0 specification for interoperable multi-vendor chiplet components. This initiative aims to drive innovation in customizable package-level integration and address future challenges in semiconductor systems.

feed.title: Micron Delivers World’s Most Advanced 176-Layer NAND Data Center SSD
feed.summary: Micron Technology has announced the sampling of the world's first vertically-integrated 176-layer NAND solid-state drive (SSD) for data centers, the Micron 7450 SSD with NVMe. This new SSD offers QoS latency below two milliseconds, a wide range of capacities from 400GB to 15.36TB, and various form factors to cater to challenging data center workloads. It integrates Micron's advanced 176-layer NAND, DRAM, internally developed SoC, and firmware, emphasizing security through features like the Secure Execution Environment (SEE) and support for Open Compute Project (OCP) deployments.

feed.title: DigitalOcean vs Cloudflare — which stock can take advantage of cloud expansion?
feed.summary: This article compares DigitalOcean Holdings (DOCN) and Cloudflare (NET), two cloud computing companies, to determine which is the better investment. DigitalOcean serves developers and SMBs, while Cloudflare focuses on web security and content delivery. The analysis concludes that Cloudflare is the less risky and better investment due to its continued large client growth and potential for SMB expansion, despite DigitalOcean's strong performance and hold in the SMB market.

feed.title: Wide Moat Stock Outlook Remains Compelling
feed.summary: The article discusses the compelling outlook for wide moat stocks, highlighting their historical outperformance, especially in rising interest rate and high inflation environments. It notes that while the VanEck Vectors Morningstar Wide Moat ETF (MOAT) is outperforming the S&P 500 year-to-date, its performance is impacted by highly valued mega-cap growth stocks, which now present opportunities to buy quality at a discount. The analysis emphasizes that wide economic moats protect companies for extended periods, contributing to long-term outperformance with less volatility.

feed.title: After clearing all regulatory hurdles, Microsoft closes $20B Nuance deal
feed.summary: Microsoft has finalized its $20 billion acquisition of Nuance Communications after successfully navigating all regulatory approvals, including those from the U.S. Justice Department, the EU, and the British Competition and Markets Authority (CMA). This move signifies Microsoft's deeper entry into the healthcare sector, with CEO Satya Nadella indicating plans to expand Nuance's AI technology beyond healthcare into other verticals like financial services and telecommunications. The CMA concluded that the acquisition would not substantially lessen competition in the healthcare transcription market.

feed.title: DXC Is Pulling Out Of Russia, Condemns ‘Unprovoked Attack On Ukraine’
feed.summary: DXC Technology announced its exit from the Russian market in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, impacting approximately 4,000 employees. The company condemned the "unprovoked attack" and stated it would no longer pursue business in Russia, while also providing support to its employees in the region, including financial assistance and relocation support. This move follows similar actions by other major IT firms and has raised concerns among solution providers about potential increases in cyberattacks.

feed.title: EA pulling games and virtual currency sales from Russia and Belarus
feed.summary: Electronic Arts (EA) has announced that it will halt the sale of its games, content, and virtual currency in Russia and Belarus across all its platforms, including regional storefronts, in-game stores, and Origin. This decision comes as a protest against the invasion of Ukraine and follows similar actions by other major game companies like Microsoft and CD Projekt. Existing players in these regions will still retain access to previously purchased titles.

feed.title: Activision CEO Bobby Kotick will leave Coca-Cola's board before Microsoft deal closes
feed.summary: Activision Blizzard CEO Bobby Kotick will not seek re-election to Coca-Cola's board of directors, a position he has held for 10 years, to focus on the impending $68.7 billion merger with Microsoft. This decision comes amidst controversy surrounding Kotick, including allegations of misconduct within Activision and scrutiny over his political funding. A non-profit investor group had previously urged Coca-Cola not to renominate Kotick due to these issues.

feed.title: Microsoft suspends all new sales of its products and services in Russia
feed.summary: Microsoft has announced its decision to suspend all new sales of its products and services in Russia, joining a growing list of companies reacting to the conflict in Ukraine. Company president and vice chair Brad Smith stated their solidarity with Ukraine, emphasizing the call for peace and protection of its people. Microsoft is also committed to protecting Ukraine's cybersecurity and supporting its Ukrainian employees.

feed.title: Consortium formed to standardize chiplet ecosystem
feed.summary: A consortium comprising major tech companies like Intel, AMD, Arm, Google Cloud, Microsoft, Qualcomm, Samsung, and TSMC has been formed to standardize the die-to-die interconnect and foster an open chiplet ecosystem. They have ratified the UCIe 1.0 specification, which provides a ubiquitous interconnect standard for package-level integration, enabling easy mixing and matching of chiplet components from multiple vendors for System-on-Chip construction. The consortium aims to address customer demand for customizable package-level integration and reduce development time and cost through open standards.

feed.title: Microsoft Vaults Further Into Health-Care Services With Closing of Nuance Deal
feed.summary: Microsoft has completed its $19.6 billion acquisition of Nuance Communications Inc., significantly expanding its presence in the health-care services market and artificial intelligence. The deal integrates Nuance's AI technology, which assists doctors in patient prediction and digital record-keeping, into Microsoft's cloud-computing and AI offerings for health care, finance, and customer service sectors. Nuance currently serves a large portion of U.S. hospitals and top financial institutions.

feed.title: How Hyperscale Data Centers are reshaping India’s IT
feed.summary: Hyperscale data centers are critical infrastructure for companies like Amazon, Google, and Microsoft, providing dedicated computing resources to handle massive user demands. These facilities are essential for the digital economy, supporting everything from emails to online shopping, and their importance has grown with trends like remote work and emerging technologies such as AI and IoT. India is poised for significant growth in its data center industry, driven by government incentives and an increasing need for robust data storage and processing capabilities, despite environmental concerns related to energy consumption.

feed.title: Electronic Arts halts all sales in Russia and Belarus
feed.summary: Electronic Arts (EA) has announced that it will cease all sales of games and content in Russia and Belarus due to the ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine. This includes sales through Origin, the EA app, and platform partners. EA also confirmed that it had previously removed Russia and Russian clubs from its FIFA and NHL 22 games and is working with partners to delist its games from stores in the affected regions.

feed.title: Microsoft closes on $16 billion acquisition of Nuance
feed.summary: Microsoft has completed its $16 billion acquisition of speech recognition company Nuance Communications. This deal, Microsoft's second-largest, aims to expand its presence in the healthcare industry through Nuance's medical dictation and transcription tools. The acquisition received clearance from British and European Union antitrust regulators after initial scrutiny.

feed.title: The Scale of Shell's Global AI Predictive Maintenance Program
feed.summary: Shell has successfully scaled its AI-driven predictive maintenance program to monitor over 10,000 pieces of equipment globally, significantly reducing operating costs, preventing downtime, and improving safety and environmental outcomes. This achievement, made possible through a partnership with C3 AI and Microsoft Azure, involves ingesting 20 billion rows of data weekly and running over 10,000 machine learning models. Shell is now making its predictive maintenance solutions commercially available through the Open AI Energy Initiative to accelerate the energy transition across the industry.

feed.title: Constellation Launches Sustainability Partnership with Microsoft featuring 24/7/365 Real-Time Carbon-Free Energy Matching Solution
feed.summary: Constellation announced a strategic five-year partnership with Microsoft to develop a 24/7/365 real-time carbon-free energy matching solution. This technology aims to help customers fully achieve their zero-emissions goals by matching real-time electricity use with local clean energy sources, offering a more precise carbon accounting method than current annual offsetting practices. Microsoft will also become an early adopter of this solution and purchase clean energy from Constellation.

feed.title: Cloud management provider Cloocus receives $41 mn in Series B funding
feed.summary: Cloud management service provider Cloocus Co. has secured $40.8 million (50 billion won) in Series B funding from SK Inc. C&C as part of a larger 100 billion won round. This investment follows significant funding rounds for other Korean cloud MSPs like Megazone Cloud and Bespin Global. The capital injections reflect a turnaround for Korean MSPs, driven by increased demand for cloud services due to the pandemic and the growing adoption of SaaS and multicloud strategies.

feed.title: Class-action lawsuit targets NBA 2K’s microtransactions
feed.summary: Take-Two Interactive, the publisher of NBA 2K22, is facing a class-action lawsuit filed by an Illinois parent regarding the game's MyTeam mode and its use of loot boxes. The lawsuit alleges "unfair, deceptive, and unlawful practices, including illegal gambling practices," and seeks over $5 million in damages. It claims these practices psychologically distance players, especially minors, from the reality of spending real money, a concern previously raised about similar systems in games like EA Sports' Ultimate Team.

feed.title: Cloudflare and Akamai to continue operations in Russia
feed.summary: Cloudflare and Akamai have stated their intention to continue operations in Russia despite calls to cease business following the invasion of Ukraine. Both companies argue that providing internet access is crucial for Russian citizens to obtain accurate information, rather than contributing to an information blackout. They have, however, condemned the invasion and ceased business with sanctioned entities or state-majority-owned customers.

feed.title: Cisco Stops Business In Russia, Ups Security Efforts In Ukraine
feed.summary: Cisco Systems has halted all business operations in Russia and Belarus in response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The company is also providing security assistance to Ukraine through its Talos threat intelligence team, offering free software auto-renewals, Webex meetings, and calls to the country. This move aligns Cisco with other major tech companies sanctioning Russia, and the company has also established a humanitarian fund for Ukraine.

feed.title: Alphabet’s (GOOGL) Stock Price Has Fallen 12.8% in 2022. Should You Buy It?
feed.summary: Alphabet's stock (GOOGL) has dropped 12.8% in 2022, leading many to question if it's a good buying opportunity. Despite plateauing ad revenues, Google is expanding into cloud services and cybersecurity, highlighted by its acquisition of Mandiant. The company is considered attractive at current prices, though antitrust concerns remain a risk.

feed.title: Telco Lumen disconnects from Russia, ends business relationships
feed.summary: Lumen Technologies, a US telecommunications company, has announced its complete disconnection from Russia due to increased security risks following the invasion of Ukraine. Initially, Lumen stopped selling new products and services to Russian entities and terminated existing agreements, and although its business interactions in Russia are not financially material, the company was a top international transit provider to the country. This move follows a similar decision by rival Cogent, leading other Russian telecommunication companies to shift to Lumen and other providers.

feed.title: Industry Leaders Join Forces to Standardize Chiplet Ecosystem
